articles.title: Brighton 4-0 Tromso (Agg: 4-0): Charalampos Kostoulas, Maxim De Cuyper, Mats Wieffer and Olivier Boscagli on target in Conference League play-off win
articles.summary: Report as Brighton qualify for the league phase of the Conference League by beating Norwegian side Tromso in second leg at the Amex; Seagulls were held in the Arctic Circle in the first leg but scored three in the first half on Thursday and can now look forward to Friday's draw
articles.body:
The Seagulls were 4-0 up against Aston Villa at the break on Sunday in the Premier League and bagged three by the interval against their Norwegian visitors here to put themselves on course for a place in Friday's draw. Olivier Boscagli then ensured it was back-to-back 4-0 wins with a late deflected drive.

The Seagulls were superb from the first whistle, overwhelming Tromso who had held them to a 0-0 draw in the Arctic Circle last week, with Charalampos Kostoulas, Maxim De Cuyper and Mats Wieffer on target in a first 45 which could easily have brought more goals.

The second half, as on Sunday, saw Brighton struggle to add to their tally but continue to boss possession. Kostoulas will be kicking himself not to have bagged many more on a night chances continually came his way but Boscagli eventually got himself on the scoresheet after he had earlier been denied by the offside flag.

Fabian Hurzeler's side have made a storming start to this season and can now look forward to the Conference League draw and then Sunday's trip to Stamford Bridge to face Chelsea, which is live on Sky Sports.

5: OVERHEAD! Charalampos Kostoulas goes for the spectacular early on from just inside the Tromso box but sends his bicycle kick off target.

22: GOAL! Kostoulas slams in to cap a dominant start from Brighton. Maxim De Cuyper wins the ball back high up the pitch and it breaks for Kostoulas, who turns, drives towards the edge of the box and then fires into the far bottom corner.

32: HUGE CHANCE! How's Pascal Gross not scored?! He couldn't get his feet sorted for De Cuyper's cutback from close range.

33: GOAL! Tromso are caught out trying to play out, as De Cuyper robs sub Leon Hien in the box and sticks the ball past Jakob Haugaard. So easy!

38: GOAL! Mats Wieffer whacks in a third! He's involved earlier in the move before switching play and when it comes back to him he's in space and able to easily convert.

50: OVER! Kostoulas shakes his head after nodding a cross over the bar. He could have had a hat-trick tonight.

61: OVER! Kostoulas with his hands on his head again! Good close control takes him away from three Tromso defenders but his blast from a tight angle is far more wild and rockets over the bar.

74: GOAL RULED OUT! Gross' shot is parried and Olivier Boscagli is quickest to react - but he's flagged offside.

76: OFF THE POST! Ibrahim Osman drives towards goal from a tight angle - but blasts against the near post. He may have been offside.

79: TROMSO SHOT! Troy Nyhammer gets in behind the Brighton defence for the first time tonight but blasts his shot at Bart Verbruggen - and then sees the offside flag go up.

86: GOAL! Boscagli finally gets his goal, driving a deflected shot into the bottom corner after Tromso on half-clear a cross.

Analysis: Free-scoring Brighton's attack set to get even stronger

Sky Sports News' Elliot Cook at the Amex:

"It's back-to-back 4-0 victories for Fabian Hurzeler's men but worth noting how many attacking absences there were through injury.

"Karou Mitoma, Stefanos Tzimas, Georginio Rutter, Evan Ferguson and Yankuba Minteh - linked with Liverpool - among them.

"When they return, Brighton will be an even stronger attacking force."

articles.title: Why Sheffield United provide the first test of the IFR's powers
articles.summary: Just a few short months ago, Sheffield Wednesday looked like providing the first real test of the powers of the new Independent Football Regulator. Now it appears it might well be Sheffield United.
articles.body:
Just a few short months ago, Sheffield Wednesday looked like being the first club to come under the microscope of the new Independent Football Regulator.

But now it is neighbours Sheffield United who are attracting the attention of the regulator.

The IFR had Wednesday in its sights when Dejphon Chansiri stopped funding the club, until administration ended his reign before the new regulator's powers kicked in. The Owls now have new owners, albeit with relegation to League One.

But for their arch rivals across the city at Bramall Lane, the IFR has said it has the power to assess the "honesty, integrity and financial soundness" of current owners and co-chairmen, Steven Rosen and Helmy Eltoukhy.

United's problems stem from a ruling at the High Court last week.

COH Sports Bidco Limited (CSBL) - the company Rosen and Eltoukhy used to buy the Blades two years ago - was wound up with an outstanding debt of £35m to the former owners, United World.

Two months ago, ownership of the club was transferred from CSBL to a new parent company, 1919 Partners LLC.

It meant CSBL, and the £35m debt, no longer had a direct link to Sheffield United.

This has left many questions and, so far, no real answers.

It is possible that the English Football League (EFL) may impose a points penalty, while the IFR - for the first time - could take action against Rosen and Eltoukhy.

How Sheffield United ended up in this situation

The Championship club have attempted to distance themselves from the saga.

It is "a matter between the current owners and former owner", according to a statement issued by the Blades after CBSL was wound up.

The club did not respond to requests for comment.

In 2009, Southampton's parent company, Southampton Leisure Holdings, went into administration. The south-coast club tried to argue it was a separate entity. An EFL investigation disagreed, with Saints docked the mandatory 10 points.

Sheffield United's situation is not quite the same, but the parallels are there.

The EFL says it will "consider the implications" of last week's developments and weigh up "whether any further action is required".

For Sheffield United fan James Kemp, better known as Blade on a Bike for this charity fundraising, it "just beggars belief".

"Do they think they can just change company names to avoid paying what they owe the previous owner?" Kemp told BBC Sport.

"It's just not the way to go about business. So in my view, I think there will be sanctions."

Regulation 12.3 allows the EFL to consider an insolvency event which happens to any company linked to the football club, like with Southampton.

If the EFL board considers CSBL to be financially connected to the Blades, the club may face the prospect of a 12-point penalty this season.

Then appendix 3, clause 10 demands advanced notice of at least 10 days for any planned transfer of ownership.

And here is where it gets more serious for the Championship club.

BBC Sport understands that neither the IFR nor the EFL were informed by Sheffield United that they were changing their ownership structure, nor that Timothy Ryan had been added to the board.

The Football Governance Act, which created the IFR, prohibits anyone from becoming an owner or director unless an application has been made and the IFR has determined they are suitable.

So this is not just about the unpaid debt, but also the transfer of assets and approval from the IFR and the EFL.

With Sheffield United not engaging it is hard to know exactly what the situation is.

So far, the narrative has been led by former owners United World, headed by Prince Abdullah, who is refusing to walk away without his money.

Rosen and Eltoukhy have not denied the unpaid £35m debt existed, and the hearing at the High Court lasted just 10 seconds before CSBL was wound up.

The Blades Fan Advisory Board, which is supposed to have regular communication with the current owners, is understandably concerned.

It has asked for information about the "transfer of ownership to 1919 Partners, the financial obligations they hold, EFL involvement in these issues and a request for wider communication with supporters".

With parachute payments having run out at the end of last season, there has been a tightening of their belts in transfers too.

The club have sold arguably their two most important players - Andre Brooks and Gustavo Hamer.

Manager Chris Wilder will have to do business in the loan and free agent market as the 1 September transfer deadline approaches.

So far, only Morecambe have come under scrutiny from the IFR. The National League North club were issued a warning notice for failing to respond to queries about the running of the club.

But this is a different level and involves serious questions about the way a Championship club have operated.

How will the IFR view the transfer from CSBL to 1919 partners? What was the process? What was the motive? And what were the financial terms to facilitate it?

And perhaps most importantly, why did the £35m debt not stay with the football club? And will this debt be paid to United World?

The IFR can impose upon a person or a club a censure statement, a fine, or place a "skilled person" in the owners' place to run the business.

Soon, the IFR will have the ability to revoke or suspend a licence to operate as a club owner - but the licensing process does not kick in until 2027-28.

Many EFL clubs have struggled financially amid a series of ownership issues across the divisions - and this led to the creation of the IFR.

Now the eyes of English football will be on how the regulator responds.

articles.title: Italy withdraws support for Infantino, but Cannavaro backs FIFA chief
articles.summary: Italian Football Federation says its decision is based on Infantino’s recent initiatives on international competitions.
articles.body:
Italy’s football federation (FIGC) has withdrawn its support for embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his failed attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

“This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC’s position… regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions,” said a FIGC statement on Wednesday.

The move comes as a host of European national associations, including England, Ireland and Wales, have already scrapped their backing of Infantino, who is seeking re-election at next year’s FIFA Congress.

Infantino has come under increasing pressure to step down as head of world football’s governing body over his now-abandoned plan to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

“We will continue to work alongside UEFA and the other European federations to promote a vision of football based on merit, solidarity, sustainability and the central role of the fans,” said FIGC head Giovanni Malago.

“We identify with a model of dialogue, listening and shared responsibility which has, to date, enabled football to grow, innovate and, at the same time, defend its founding principles.”

However, Italy’s World Cup-winning captain, Fabio Cannavaro, and his Brazilian counterpart, Cafu, have joined a group of former footballers backing Infantino.

Their social media messages expressing support came after another group of former players, led by Frenchman Mikael Silvestre, called for “change” in FIFA’s leadership.

“Over the last ten years, world football has improved,” and footballers “have once again taken centre stage,” Cannavaro – who was part of Italy’s 2006 World Cup-winning team, posted on social media on Wednesday.

“Infantino has done a great job… Not acknowledging that would be intellectually dishonest,” added the former centre-back, who coaches the Uzbekistan national team.

Similar messages were posted on Tuesday night by Brazilians Cafu and Roberto Carlos, Argentines Javier Zanetti and Esteban Cambiasso, Colombia’s Ivan Ramiro Cordoba and Mexico’s Jared Borgetti.

“We have followed the work of FIFA and president Infantino to promote the representation of players in football, something that didn’t exist before,” wrote Cafu, who lifted the World Cup with Brazil in 1994 and 2002.

Infantino, the 56-year-old former UEFA secretary general, had the broad backing of European nations when he succeeded Sepp Blatter as FIFA president in 2016.

European football body UEFA said it would formally withdraw its threat to boycott FIFA competitions after receiving assurances that Infantino’s failed sell-off plan will not be revived.

UEFA, which oversees European football, had threatened to boycott FIFA competitions.

articles.title: Mou quiere más
articles.standfirst: Contento con el juego ofensivo del Madrid, su objetivo ahora es potenciar la defensa
articles.summary: Contento con el juego ofensivo del Madrid, su objetivo ahora es potenciar la defensa
articles.body: De momento las cosas van bien para el Real Madrid de José Mourinho 2.0. Pero el técnico quiere más, sobre todo en defensa. Los dos goles encajados en los dos primeros partidos de Liga incomodan al técnico portugués, que pretende mejorar el blindaje del equipo, consciente de que el potencial del ataque será difícil de contener para la mayoría de los rivales de los blancos a lo largo de la temporada. A Mou no le han gustado los dos goles encajados, ante Espanyol y Real, ni el momento en que han llegado, poco después de que los blancos se adelantaran en el marcador. La falta de concentración después de hacer lo más difícil, que siempre es marcar el primer gol, es uno de los aspectos a mejorar por parte del equipo, que ante la Real concedió tres tiros a puerta. Sólo uno acabó en gol, pero los donostiarras sumaron un total de 10 intentos sobre la meta de Courtois (siete fuera), una cifra considerada mejorable por parte del técnico de Setúbal. El sábado pasado en Cornellá, el Espanyol también firmó tres remates a la portería de Courtois, de un total de ocho. De ahí que Mou considere clave mejorar el balance defensivo del equipo, una tarea que no recae sólo en los zagueros. Para el técnico, defender es un trabajo colectivo, que debe implicar a los once futbolistas sobre el terreno de juego, del portero al delantero centro. En el otro lado de la balanza, el equipo está demostrando el potencial ofensivo que se le suponía. Ante el Espanyol realizó 21 remates, ocho a puerta, y 20 ante la Real, un total de 10 entre los tres palos. En total, seis goles y dos disparos a la madera (Bellingham y Fede en Barcelona) que acreditan la potencia de fuego de los madrileños, pese a la escasez de rodaje colectivo a estas alturas del mes de agosto. En resumen, Mou está satisfecho con lo que ve. El equipo ha dominado la posesión en estos dos primeros partidos (aunque sólo 51-49 ante la Real), un dato que el técnico portugués siempre ha relativizado. Para Mou, no se trata tanto de cantidad como de calidad. Y el equipo está generando ocasiones al nivel de lo esperado, siempre con el amplio margen de mejora propio de estas alturas de la temporada. Con independencia del seis de seis, algo anecdótico con tan sólo dos jornadas disputadas, el equipo carbura y va mejorando de forma progresiva tras los cuatros tests de pretemporada y los dos primeros partidos oficiales del curso. Y, mientras se construye, gana, lo que siempre facilita las cosas de puertas afuera y eleva la confianza del vestuario en el nuevo proyecto.

articles.title: El Girona hace oficial el traspaso de Tsygankov al Ajax
articles.standfirst: Acaba uno de los culebrones del verano entre el club catalán y el ucraniano con Míchel al rescate
articles.summary: Acaba uno de los culebrones del verano entre el club catalán y el ucraniano con Míchel al rescate
articles.body: El Girona se ha sacado una de las piedras que se ha encontrado en el camino en su planificación de la plantilla para este curso 2026/27, en el que vuelve a Segunda y él mismo, como recién descendido, se ha colgado la etiqueta de favorito al ascenso. Y habrá que verlo porque los múltiples cambios en el plantel que se esperan en las últimas horas de mercado no serán fáciles de digerir. De momento, los blanquirrojos se han sacado de encima uno de los jugadores en rebeldía que no ha querido ni jugar amistosos durante la pretemporada ni, por consiguiente, ninguno de los dos partidos oficiales de liga. Viktor Tsygankov ya es historia en el Girona después que el Ajax haya alcanzado un acuerdo de traspaso por el futbolista con los catalanes a cambio de unos 3,5 millones de euros más uno en variables y un porcentaje de una futura venda. Míchel volverá a tener a sus órdenes un futbolista de gran calidad, pero con números por debajo de los esperados en el club de Montilivi. Los gerundenses pues, dejan atrás un verano con el ucraniano que no ha sido de buen grado para nadie, con un acto de indisciplina del futbolista negándose a cambiarse con sus compañeros en la primera jornada de liga en Montilivi contra el Leganés y, posteriormente, haciendo públicos Tsygankov unos mensajes privados con un trabajador del club en redes sociales que le costaron un expediente disciplinario. El extremo llegó el invierno del 2023 al Girona por 5 M€ procedente del Dinamo de Kiev, que guardaba el 50% de plusvalía del jugador, algo que no va a cobrar porqué la venta se ha hecho por debajo del valor de compra. Vanat, otro de los tres ucranianos que quedan en el Girona junto a Krapyvtsov y Pyshchur, borró todas las fotos relacionadas con la ciudad de Girona y de él como futbolista del club. Una clara alusión a que la molestias que le impidieron jugar ante el Córdoba en la segunda jornada quizás fueron algo más que un percance físico. Veremos porque si el ariete se va, el problemón para la dirección deportiva será muy grande ya que se tendrá que comprar un nueve de referencia titular a pocas horas del cierre. Estrés en las oficinas ya que también están en el alambre el futuro de Ounahi, Asprilla, Bryan Gil y Van de Beek. Tremendo. "El Girona FC y el AFC Ajax han llegado a un acuerdo para el traspaso de Viktor Tsygankov", es lo único que comentó el club al respecto tras el largo tira y afloja entre ambas partes durante este verano.

articles.title: David Moyes: Is Everton boss on same page as club's owners?
articles.summary: David Moyes said he was surprised Everton's owners regarded missing out on Europe last season as "failure". Phil McNulty asks if they are they on the same page.
articles.body:
Everton 's owners the Friedkin Group are rarely seen and barely heard – so when they announced via chief executive Angus Kinnear that they regarded missing out on European football last season as "failure" it came as a surprise.

Everton were in one of the nine European places on offer to English clubs when Merlin Rohl gave them the lead against Sunderland in their penultimate game of last season.

Instead, in keeping with a collapse that saw them fail to win any of their last seven league games, Everton lost 3-1 at home to the Europe-bound Black Cats, before a final-day defeat at Tottenham Hotspur left them in 13th place.

In an interview with BBC Radio Merseyside, Kinnear said: "They viewed it as a failure because it was a failure.

"The Friedkins are winners. They want to win and we didn't win anything."

Moyes' response when this was put to him was intriguing – and begs the question whether the 63-year-old Scot is on the same page as Everton 's American powerbrokers - who also own Italian club Roma - when it comes to ambition.

He said: "I'm surprised they were disappointed because there was never, ever any time anyone said to me 'David, you have to make Europe or you have to be in and around the top end'.

"I think everybody wanted to make sure we moved into the new stadium safe and with not having too difficult a season and we certainly did that last year."

Kinnear also said: "We have definitely had discussions with the ownership and David about how we use the Carabao Cup and FA Cup to give the fans something to really cheer and get behind."

Former Everton and England midfield man Leon Osman told BBC Sport: "I was a bit surprised at the statement and at the timing because, as Moyes said, I don't think anyone was saying for much of last season that not getting into Europe was a failure.

"I do think when you get on the cusp of something and it slips away, it can feel like you've failed, but I would call it a disappointment rather than a failure because so often in the last five years, before David Moyes took over, Everton have been trying to keep their heads above water by staying in the Premier League."

He added: "Of course everyone associated with Everton was disappointed because excitement was building but take a step back and look at clubs who did get into Europe, like Brighton and Bournemouth . They have been building steadily over years to put themselves in the position to make that last stride.

"I think Everton have done good business this summer and maybe if they can do more before the close of the window they might be in a better position to make that step."

Moyes bristled, questioning whether journalists were "dead stupid" when asked about the importance of cup competitions, and spirits will have been lifted by the convincing second-round Carabao Cup win at Preston North End.

Kinnear said in the same interview that Everton 's squad was "in a good place" – although added there was work to do.

Moyes sounded a markedly more cautious note, warning fans not to get carried away with an opening Premier League win against Crystal Palace and victory at Deepdale.

It is clear Moyes wants TFG to deliver more backing before the transfer window closes to improve, and bolster, a squad which ran out of steam so badly last season.

He said: "For us to be a side which is competitive, I still think we have got a lot of work to do. Hopefully we are able to try and do some of it.

"We need more players. Our squad is not big enough and we need to get more quality in some areas if we can do.

"I'm not sure we will, but it's not for me and the want of trying, that's for sure."

The messages were certainly mixed, adding to a summer of mixed fortunes in the transfer market, that even led to Prime Minister and fanatical Evertonian Andy Burnham to comment on one of the hot topics when he said: "There is one thing I would just ask, sign a right-back."

This is what makes the final few days of the transfer window so vital for Moyes, who is in the final year of his contract, and Everton .

And it will not simply be about incomings. Moyes will be desperate to hang on to Iliman Ndiaye, the inspirational forward who has been central to his plans.

Everton have signed the PFA Championship player of the year Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough. Christian Norgaard will provide experience from Arsenal as a replacement for departed veteran Idrissa Gueye, while deals for young German Merlin Rohl and England under-21 winger Tyrique George, on loan last season, were confirmed. Brennan Johnson arrived from Crystal Palace in a straight swap with Dwight McNeil.

Moyes, however, makes it plain he does not think this is enough.

So now Everton 's fans must wait to see if owners, chief executive and manager can reach a meeting of minds to give Moyes what he wants and demonstrate exactly what TFG's ambitions are.

Dan Friedkin, the club's billionaire chairman, has not attended any Everton games and while absences are not uncommon among American owners, there still lurks a suspicion among Toffees' fans that TFG's interest is more piqued by their Serie A giants Roma, who are in the Champions League.

And despite such a promising start, questions still remain, especially that vexed matter of a right-back that has become such a bone of contention among Everton fans.

Moyes is believed to favour Strasbourg's Guela Doue, but this appears to have fallen down on financial grounds.

A move for Celtic's Canada right-back Alistair Johnston stalled when he got injured. Crystal Palace 's Daniel Munoz was considered but as yet not pursued. Fulham would not entertain interest in Timothy Castagne. Aaron Wan-Bissaka was another considered but he joined Aston Villa on loan from West Ham United.

Eventually - surely - all parties will have to agree on a target and finally address this obvious flaw.

The £7m move for 32-year-old Norgaard looks smart work at a decent price, although Everton were hopeful of signing fellow Danish midfielder Morten Hjulmand from Sporting in Lisbon until Atletico Madrid stepped in.

Hackney is a classic Moyes signing, an outstanding Championship performer in the mould of those who arrived at Everton during his first spell such as Tim Cahill, Phil Jagielka and Joleon Lescott, as well as at West Ham United, when he signed Jarrod Bowen from Hull City .

Moyes clearly believes he needs more, especially as he will be well aware that he took the brunt of heavy fan criticism when Europe slipped away last season, and will look to TFG to bring him what he feels he needs.

TFG has delivered financial stability after the mayhem of the Farhad Moshiri years and has spent about £170m on players, so for this it deserves credit.

Osman added: "There will be constant noise until the right-back is signed and plenty would probably like a new number nine as well, but looking at the rest of the squad I think the club and David have done brilliant business.

"It takes five or six transfer windows minimum to get there depending on your starting point, so there is a few to go yet on that basis, so of course these last days of the window are important and you can absolutely see why David would like more players and quality in."

Moyes has made his views clear. Now can his wish align with Everton 's owners to deliver?

articles.title: "Hay 60.000 personas insultando a tu madre, a tu familia, a tus hijos..."
articles.standfirst: Guendouzi, centrocampista del Fenerbahçe, explica su polémico comportamiento hacia la grada de Lyon tras el partido de Champions League
articles.summary: Guendouzi, centrocampista del Fenerbahçe, explica su polémico comportamiento hacia la grada de Lyon tras el partido de Champions League
articles.body: "60.000 personas están insultando a tu madre, a tu familia, a tus hijos y nadie les dice que se callen". Así explicaba Matteo Guendouzi (Poissi, 1999), centrocampista francés del Fenerbahçe, sus gestos de provocación hacia la afición del Olympique Lyon tras la victoria turca en el partido decisivo que daba el pase al sorteo grande de la Champions League. La celebración turca sobre el césped derivó en una tangana que se extendió al túnel de vestuarios cuando Guendouzi se dedicó a dirigirse a la afición francesa. En una de las imágenes se ve al jugador llevarse las manos a la zona genital. Jugadores del Lyon le fueron a recriminar su comportamiento y miembros de las dos entidades se enfrentaron dentro y fuera de la hierba. Guendouzi adornó también sus gestos con gritos en los que reivindicaba su devoción por el Olympique de Marsella, uno de los grandes rivales de la entidad de Lyon. El centrocampista gritó una y otra vez 'Allez l'OM, allez l'OM'. El futbolista reconoció en las últimas horas que esos gritos estaban justificados por sus colores: "Nunca he escondido que soy aficionado del Marsella". Para Guendouzi, pivote titular del Fenerbahçe, el verano se presenta movido después de estos incidentes. El futbolista, del que se esperaba una carrera rutilante, ha probado en diferentes grandes Ligas sin haber encontrado en ningún momento la estabilidad. Dotado de buena técnica, nunca ha llegado a donde se le esperaba. Con 27 años ya ha vestido las camisetas de Lorient, Arsenal, Hertha de Berlín, Olympique de Marsella, Lazio y la actual del Fenerbahce. Con la selección francesa disputó el Mundial de Qatar. Ahora esperará cómo resuelve la UEFA los incidentes de la noche del miércoles en Lyon.

articles.title: El Atlético insiste: No se negociará el traspaso de Julián al Barça
articles.standfirst: Respaldo absoluto del Consejo de Administración del Atlético a la postura con el tema del argentino
articles.summary: Respaldo absoluto del Consejo de Administración del Atlético a la postura con el tema del argentino
articles.body: “Algunos pueden engañar a mucha gente durante mucho tiempo, pero es imposible engañar a todos todo el tiempo”. resumen en la entidad para explicar la situación de un Julián que por segundo día consecutivo no se presentó a los entrenamientos. Una posición de fuerza que topa con la voluntad firme de los rojiblancos de no vender al jugador al Barça, Una decisión que cuenta con el respaldo unánime del Consejo de Administración a la estrategia del club Y es que los miembros del Consejo de Administración del Atlético de Madrid han mostrado de forma unánime su absoluto respaldo a la decisión del club de no negociar el traspaso de Julián Alvarez al Fútbol Club Barcelona. Los miembros del Consejo de Administración son conscientes de que “el Atlético de Madrid está abierto a las negociaciones propias del mercado de transferencias, pero siempre de una forma ética y profesional y con respeto entre los clubes. Respaldamos completamente la posición previamente comunicada por el club de que el Fútbol Club Barcelona no ha cumplido con estos requisitos y por consecuencia ni ha existido ni va a existir ninguna negociación con ellos en relación al traspaso de Julián Alvarez”. El Atlético de Madrid está convencido de que el jugador comprenderá la decisión, centrándose en trabajar de la mejor manera para ayudar al club a cumplir sus objetivos, como ya lo ha hecho en las dos temporadas que ha estado defendiendo nuestros colores. En Mónaco el mundo del fútbol europeo se reúne con motivo del sorteo de la Champions. Reunión de EFC y muy comentada la forma de actuar del Barcelona, que no ha cumplido la norma habitual de los clubes. La gestión de Fernando Hidalgo y Laporta, insisten en el club, se considera un ridículo histórico y se está comentando mucho entre los clubes que se han dado cita en Mónaco.

articles.summary: It's not uncommon for there to be a wealth of college football talent returning, but 2026 seems a bit abnormal, even by lofty standards. With NIL making it worth upperclassmen's while to return, there's an uptick in returning talent.
articles.body:
It's not uncommon for there to be a wealth of college football talent returning, but 2026 seems a bit abnormal, even by lofty standards. With NIL making it worth upperclassmen's while to return, there's an uptick in returning talent.

The Heisman Trophy winner is gone, but there are still plenty of All-Americans, key contributors and rising stars ready to take Fernando Mendoza's baton and run with it.

As always, the SEC dominates the individual player talent market, but the Big Ten is top-heavy in terrific teams. Both of the nation's top conferences have plenty of representation here.

Everybody's list will be different, and while production is key, there's also some weight applied to those expected to do big things with either expanded roles or more experience. Regardless, there are plenty of reasons to be excited about those who made the list and heaping the hype on those who could play their way onto it.

Much of the talent may reside in the SEC, but the reason why the Big Ten could win a fourth straight national championship is a loaded crop of quarterbacks. When you've got proven field generals, you're halfway to winning the battle.

Nobody is more hyped than Oregon's Dante Moore , who spurned millions to return to Eugene. Perhaps his top competition for the Heisman Trophy will come from the same league in the form of Ohio State's Julian Sayin , who should take a massive leap in Year 2 under center for the Buckeyes.

The SEC counters with Texas junior Arch Manning , who belongs in the top-tier conversation alongside Moore and Sayin, as does Ole Miss' breakout star Trinidad Chambliss .

Rounding out the best of the bunch are Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Miami's Darian Mensah – who left Duke for the national runners-up late in the portal process.

If you want some names of Tier 2 signal-callers who could wedge their way in, Indiana's Josh Hoover , LSU's Sam Leavitt , South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers , USC's Jayden Maiava , Georgia's Gunner Stockton , Washington's Demond Williams , Arizona's Noah Fifita , Utah's Devon Dampier , SMU's Kevin Jennings , BYU's Bear Bachmeier and Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker aren't far behind.

The nation's top two runners reside in the SEC with Missouri's Ahmad Hardy and former Tiger (and current Ole Miss star) Kewan Lacy leading the way.

Hardy will have to wait to take the field as he recovers from a gunshot wound suffered this offseason.

He may not be the flashiest, but few meant more to his team in last year's College Football Playoff than Miami heart-and-soul star Mark Fletcher Jr. He and Louisville's Isaac Brown help the ACC enter the conversation, and BYU's LJ Martin is a volume back, too.

Some underappreciated mass-producers are Texas Tech's Cameron Dickey , Texas' Hollywood Smothers , Duke's Nate Sheppard and Florida's Jadan Baugh .

You know what you're getting from steady vets like Georgia Tech transfer Justice Haynes , Georgia's Nate Frazier , Michigan's Jordan Marshall and Tennessee senior Desean Bishop , and youngsters like Oregon's Dierre Hill Jr., Ohio State's Bo Jackson and Oklahoma State's Caleb Hawkins have the potential to be the nation's best backs, too.

We all love the playmakers with pizzazz, and you don't get that anywhere better than on the perimeter.

That's where Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith rules the day, holding down the top spot in many publications' player rankings, regardless of position. But there are others on his heels.

With Arch Manning throwing him the ball, Cam Coleman could finally show everybody his ridiculous talent as a junior. It's on the same physical level as Smith's, and now he's got a stage. There weren't many who took that stage and performed better than Miami's Malachi Toney as a true freshman a season ago. What's he have in store for an encore?

With KC Concepcion gone from Texas A&M, Mario Craver steps into the spotlight, and it's also time for Alabama's Ryan Coleman-Williams to match the hype he displayed as a freshman a couple of seasons ago. Oklahoma's Isaiah Sategna III makes the Sooners' offense tick.

Big-bodied pass-catchers KJ Duff (Rutgers), Duce Robinson (Florida State) and Deondre Johnson (Jacksonville State) are stars, as are Ryan Wingo (Texas) and Amare Thomas (Houston).

There are deadly combos elsewhere, too. Oregon ( Dakorien Moore / Evan Stewart ), Indiana ( Nick Marsh / Charlie Becker ), Tennessee ( Braylon Staley / Mike Matthews ) and Clemson ( Antonio Williams / Bryant Wesco Jr. / T.J. Moore ) have star-studded groups who could shine, too.

LSU already boasts one of the nation's top tight ends in Trey'Dez Green , and coach Lane Kiffin already has shown he knows how to use an elite player at the position.

That would be crazy, but what's also bonkers is the level of tight end talent this year.

Texas Tech's Terrance Carter Jr. and Oregon's Jamari Johnson are pro prospects who are primed for big-time seasons for national title contenders. Then in the Big Ten, you've got Penn State's Benjamin Brahmer and Iowa's DJ Vonnahme who are All-American candidates.

The ACC (Virginia Tech's Luke Reynolds ) and Big 12 (UCF's Dylan Wade ) enter the conversation for the top player at the position, too. This could be a year where quarterbacks are hitting the big men, not because they're safety valves but because they're home-run threats.

With five positions to cover, there are going to be several dudes on this list, but even though there may not be a lot of sure-fire early picks in the NFL draft, this is a deep, strong group.

At center, it's really a two-man race for the nation's best with Iowa's Kade Pieper shifting inside after Logan Jones left for the NFL and Georgia veteran Drew Bobo leading the way.

The guards may even get less love, but those road-graders are bountiful in college football's '26 crop, too. Notre Dame's Anthonie Knapp shifts inside to make room for Will Black , and he will be among the nation's top interior linemen.

Joining him on the list are Cincinnati's Evan Tengesdahl , Houston's Shadre Hurst , Ohio State's Luke Montgomery , Minnesota's Greg Johnson , Oregon's Iapani Lalolu and Dave Iuli , Alabama's Michael Carroll and Washington's John Mills .

At tackle, though, is where the pro prospects really stand out. Texas' Trevor Goosby dodged major injury news but still is dealing with a knee bone bruise to open the season. The Longhorns need one of the nation's best blind-side blockers back.

Indiana veteran Carter Smith , LSU transfer Jordan Seaton , Missouri's Cayden Green , Georgia's Earnest Greene III , Ohio State's Austin Siereveld and SMU's PJ Williams lead the top group. South Carolina's Jaccarius Peak , Iowa's Trevor Lauck and Michigan's Andrew Sprague are other potential maulers on the outside.

These days, the distinction between an edge-rusher, defensive end and outside linebacker can be blurry. But the nation's best players at those positions appear on the next two slides.

When it comes to guys who can get after the quarterback, this year's crop is deep, led by Texas' Colin Simmons , South Carolina's Dylan Stewart , Michigan's John Henry Daley , Oregon's Matayo Uiagalelei , Louisville's Clev Lubin and Minnesota's Anthony Smith .

Texas Tech loaded up on defensive linemen in the portal again, and former San Diego State star Trey White may be the best of the bunch. Elsewhere, Damon Wilson II (Missouri to Miami) and Princewill Umanmielen (Ole Miss to LSU) were also among the portal's marquee edge-rusher additions.

Others like Arkansas' Quincy Rhodes Jr. , Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore and Clemson's Will Heldt round out a deep group.

Then there's the beef in the middle. Oregon's A'Mauri Washington , Ole Miss' Will Echoles , Georgia's Elijah Griffin , Texas Tech's A.J. Holmes and Oklahoma's David Stone may be the best.

Tyrique Tucker and Mario Landino give Indiana a stout tandem. Miami's Ahmad Moten Sr. , Kentucky's Tavion Gadson , Tennessee's Xavier Gilliam and USC's Jahkeem Stewart also stand out, with Stewart poised for a breakout season.

If a defense doesn't have a strong second level, it's nearly impossible to be effective. The linebacker position isn't quite as valued in the NFL as it used to be, but in the college game, there's nothing like a sideline-to-sideline star.

Much like at the edge position, Texas may have the best of the bunch in Pittsburgh transfer Rasheem Biles , who is primed for a monster season. But he's in a loaded SEC that also includes Auburn's Xavier Atkins , Ole Miss' Suntarine Perkins , the Georgia duo of Raylen Wilson and Chris Cole , Alabama's Yhonzae Pierre , Tennessee's Arion Carter and LSU's Whit Weeks .

We'll hear plenty from Notre Dame in the secondary slide, but linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa is as good as any at his position, and Drayk Bowen will complement him nicely.

Ben Roberts takes the mantle from Jacob Rodriguez in Lubbock for Texas Tech, Sammy Brown is a stalwart at Clemson and Rolijah Hardy is an All-America candidate at Indiana.

Oregon's Tietum Tuioti and BYU transfer Cade Uluave belong in the conversation, too. A lot of these guys will be playing on Sundays very soon, but we'll have the treat of watching them on collegiate gridirons first.

The stoutest position in all of college football might just be the secondary, where there are waves of superstar players.

That may seem hard to believe, but there are too many ball hawks to mention across the sport.

None is better than Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore , who leads a stacked defensive backfield in South Bend that also includes Braunte Johnson, Adon Shuler, Tae Johnson and Christian Gray .

Other teams are loaded on the back end, too. Georgia ( KJ Bolden/Ellis Robinson IV ), Oregon ( Brandon Finney Jr./Koi Perich ), Alabama ( Bray Hubbard/Zabien Brown ), LSU ( Ty Benefield and DJ Pickett ) and Oklahoma ( Peyton and Eli Bowen ) have multiple stars.

Minnesota's John Nestor , Mississippi State's Kelley Jones , Indiana's Jamari Sharpe , Miami's Bryce Fitzgerald and Clemson's Amare Ferrell are potential All-Americans, too.

There's just a lot to love about this year's college football crop of stars.

articles.summary: It may seem difficult to believe, but college football is back. A handful of other intriguing games will follow as the NCAA provides its proverbial appetizer to next week's main course.
articles.body:
It may seem difficult to believe, but college football is back. Week 0 will officially kick off on Saturday when North Carolina and TCU do battle in Aviva Stadium in Dublin, Ireland. A handful of other intriguing games will follow as the NCAA provides its proverbial appetizer to next week's main course.

Week 1 is set to begin on Thursday, September 3.

In addition to the opener in Ireland, fans will see No. 14 USC in Week 0 action, plus an underrated matchup between Jacksonville State and North Dakota State.

Here, you'll find a look at what's ahead, including scheduling information, odds, predictions, and the latest forecast information from The Weather Channel .

Schedule: 12 p.m. ET on ESPN and Disney+

Jacksonville State (+7.5) at North Dakota State

Prediction: North Dakota State 30, Jacksonville State 20

Sacramento State (+9.5) at Eastern Michigan

Prediction: Eastern Michigan 28, Sacramento State 23

Forecast: Clear to Partly Cloudy, Low of 57°F

New Mexico State (+30.5) at Florida State

Forecast: Scattered Thunderstorms, Low of 71°F

Prediction: Florida State 48, New Mexico State 17

While Week 0 isn't loaded with marquee matchups or top-25 teams, fans will be treated to some meaningful action.

The day's opener might not feature title contenders, but it will likely serve as a talking point in the following week. After a 4-8 debut season, Bill Belichick is desperately trying to turn around his heavily hyped North Carolina program.

The Tarheels have generated far more drama off the field than on it during Belichick's tenure—the latest development seeing GM Michael Lombardi being placed on administrative leave —but winning can cure plenty. The question is whether North Carolina can win against a quality TCU team that thumped the Tarheels 48-14 in last year's opener.

The Horned Frogs are rightfully favored here, though an improved North Carolina roster (on paper) and possible rainfall should keep this one closer than last year's matchup.

USC enters Week 0 as a top-25 team and a potential College Football Playoff (CFP) contender. Head coach Lincoln Riley and quarterback Jayden Maiava are back and looking to improve upon last year's 9-4 record. The Trojans were 7-2 in Big Ten play last year but went 2-3 against ranked opponents and missed the CFP.

San Jose State will largely serve as a tune-up opponent for USC, but the game should give fans an early glimpse at a Trojans squad looking to make noise in the playoff race.

After a soft early schedule, USC will face potential title contenders in Oregon, Ohio State, and Indiana.

The midday matchup between Jacksonville State and North Dakota State might not be on the radar of many casual fans, but it should be a fun one for those who tune in.

This game will mark North Dakota State's FBS debut as the program officially joins the Mountain West. The Bison won a whopping 10 championships at the FCS level and will now test their ability against FBS competition—Jacksonville State made the leap in 2023—in quarterback Nathan Hayes's first career start.

"It's super exciting, but we just put our heads down and work," Hayes told James McCarthy of Flag Family Media.

The Bison will be worth tracking in 2026 because it is immediately eligible for the CFP. This offseason, the Division I Cabinet voted to eliminate the two-year transition penalty for teams making the FCS-to-FBS jump. North Dakota State and Sacramento State are making that jump in 2026 and will be playoff-eligible if they meet all other CFP requirements.

Saturday's nightcap will bring another potentially CFP-relevant matchup between Memphis and UNLV. Both programs head into 2026 with a chance to represent the Group of Six in the playoff.

With the Pac-12 rebranded as a non-power conference, the Group of Five has been upgraded to a six-conference field. At the end of the regular season, the highest-ranked G6 team will earn a playoff bid.

Memphis is among the preseason ACC favorites, while UNLV is a slight favorite (+260) in the Mountain West over North Dakota State (+320). The ACC, Mountain West, Pac-12, MAC, Sun Belt, and C-USA now comprise the Group of Six.

articles.summary: Hello, bonjour, olá!
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live blog for the 2026-26 UEFA Champions League league phase draw.

Your host, Leo Collis, is here to provide updates so you don't have to sit through the slog that is the ceremony process (you're welcome).

Which teams will be facing off in marquee matches? And, crucially, which retired footballers will be put through excruciatingly cringy interviews in between balls being picked?

With all 36 participating teams now confirmed following the final round of qualification matches last night, the race to the June final at the Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid is set to begin in earnest, with the first games kicking off on September 8.

And that's that! Full details of the fixtures can be found on the UEFA Champions League website .

The reigning European champions will take on Barcelona at Le Parc des Princes, making a tricky matchup a little more palatable for the French side.

Lamine Yamal versus Nuno Mendes on the wing will be a fascinating contest, while trying to marshal Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele and Desire Doue will be a big test for the rising Pau Cubarsi.

In the league phase last season, a weakened PSG team came away with a 2-1 win, so the Blaugrana will want to atone for that.

The German champions will take on the English champions, with Bayern handling hosting duties.

Arsenal got the better of Bayern Munich in the league phase last year, claiming a 3-1 with goals from Jurrien Timber, Noni Madueke and Gabriel Martinelli. Lennart Karl got the consolation at the Emirates.

That home swing in Bayern's favor should make a big difference, and the Gunners' rock-solid defense will need to figure out how to keep Harry Kane, Luis Diaz and Michael Olise quiet.

Liverpool and Atletico Madrid will once again meet on the European stage, and the English side will be delighted it's not in the elimination stages (yet).

The Reds have got the better of Los Rojiblancos in the last three meetings in the opening UCL round, but a last-16 exit to the La Liga side in 2019-20 still stings.

Atleti will bring the fight to Anfield, and a brittle Liverpool defense might not be able to handle the pressure.

Jose Mourinho will relish facing off against Arsenal once again, having done so frequently while manager of Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur.

Real Madrid's depth of talent on offer can be rivaled by Arsenal's impressive squad, and it should result in a chess-match-style fixture with the potential to explode any minute.

A meeting of two clubs backed by petrostates will be combustible.

While PSG have backed away from a high-spending model in recent years, City have continued to put their money where their mouth is, spending over $250 million on two players in this summer's window alone.

They've not met since the league phase in 2024-25, when PSG came away with a 4-2 win. Much has changed since then, so it will be intriguing to see how they stack up against one another now.

articles.title: Expert CFB Betting Locks for TCU vs. North Carolina and Week 0's Biggest Games
articles.summary: Oh, it's been a journey.
articles.body:
To arrive here, at actual football games, we've had to endure another dreadful offseason. From courtrooms to NIL drama to College Football Playoff expansion rumors, we've crawled through the mess that is the college football offseason.

None of it is all that fun or interesting, if we're being honest. But that doesn't change a thing.

College football—actual, beautiful football—is back.

Per tradition here at Bleacher Report, we will dissect each and every week of the college football season, picking games against the spread all season long. We'll keep a season-long tally, documenting our successes (and failures).

Hopefully many more successes than failures.

We kick things off with Week 0, an abbreviated slate but one still so full of promise. Don't let the lack of games fool you; there is money to be made.

Bill Belichick enters the 2026 season amid pressure to deliver at North Carolina.

And let's not forget about this matchup last year. The Horned Frogs won 48-14, and the game was over shortly after it began. As such, the masses will likely flock to bet TCU, laying more than a touchdown with ease.

To a certain degree, I get it. Things at North Carolina likely eventually won't end well, and it feels like the clock is ticking. With that acknowledged, the Tar Heels played a slew of tight games late in the season, showing massive improvements along the way.

What does that mean exactly? Given how much movement the sport experiences these days, probably not much. But it's worth noting regardless.

What does feel likely, however, is that the two quarterbacks in this game surprise.

Billy Edwards Jr. will get the nod for UNC, and he has a wealth of experience to lean on. Working with Bobby Petrino, for as odd as that hire felt, should be an enormous boost for an offense that needs it.

On the other side, TCU will start Jaden Craig. The Harvard transfer was a fascinating addition and has earned some rave reviews.

Neither offense is likely to dominate, and both QBs could surprise. Expect both teams to put on a show in Ireland.

Somehow, Stanford has played its way into being only a small home favorite against a Hawai'i team that had hit rock bottom not terribly long ago.

Under Timmy Chang, however, the Rainbow Warriors have found life. They have found tempo. They have found offense. And it all translated into a sensational nine-win season last fall.

In many respects, that's why the line sits where it does. It's also why Stanford, despite being favored, likely won't be a public darling for anyone betting on more than name alone.

For Stanford, this team has Andrew Luck's fingerprints all over it. It's not the final version. Heck, it's not anything close to it. But the head coach, Tavita Pritchard, was handpicked and the personnel and playing style should look and feel more like the Stanford of old.

As for the quarterback, he will not be intimidated by the stage. Before suffering a torn ACL in Michigan's ReliaQuest Bowl win over Alabama on Dec. 31, 2024, Davis Warren faced five ranked opponents during the regular season: No. 3 Texas, No. 11 USC, No. 8 Oregon, No. 13 Indiana and No. 2 Ohio State.

He will not be intimidated by the stage. Look for Stanford to play ball control and for Warren to make just enough plays to deliver a win (and cover).

What a year for Virginia it was. The Cavaliers lost only three football games last season, and the three losses came by a combined 18 points.

It's worth noting, though, that three wins came in overtime and two others came by a touchdown or less. This team largely thrived in big games, even if it wasn't always pretty or easy.

Which leads us to a fascinating opener against a fascinating opponent.

In many respects, the quarterbacks should be the focal point of any game. In this particular matchup, it feels even more relevant.

In the year of the quarterback, CJ Bailey and Beau Pribula aren't exactly fixtures. Still, both can be incredibly productive players, and Bailey possesses some pretty spectacular skills (and size) that makes one wonder why he isn't a bigger deal nationally.

He'll have many new weapons to work with, and the loss of running back Hollywood Smothers really stings. But Bailey is just so capable regardless of his targets.

In a game that will likely feature plenty of action on the chalk—and perhaps for good reason—we are cozying up to NC State. We wouldn't be shocked if the Wolfpack delivered an outright winner, either.

North Dakota State (-7) vs. Jacksonville State

The Bison are making this massive leap after losing four games only once in 15 seasons at the FCS level. Over that same span, they finished with one or fewer losses in nine seasons.

To say this has been one of the most dominant teams in all of football, at any level, would be an understatement.

With that acknowledged, this is a slippery opponent to open the year. Jacksonville State. Since 2022, the Gamecocks have won nine games in every season, doing so in a variety of ways. Last year, Jacksonville State was third in the nation in rushing yards, averaging 5.31 yards per carry for the year.

Even with new offensive coordinator Taylor Housewright calling plays, expect that still to be the strategy.

Candidly, evaluating games like this early on is challenging. NIL has made roster turnover across the sport the norm, thus the evaluation process becomes more difficult. For rosters of this stature, the turnover and departures are even more significant.

In the end, we're siding with consistency. We're backing new starter Nathan Hayes, who has plenty of snaps despite serving as a backup.

The nightcap for Week 0 features two very capable non-Power Four teams with genuine playoff aspirations.

For Memphis, this will be the start of the Charles Huff era. Former head coach Ryan Silverfield is now at Arkansas, which means Huff will get his turn. We don't know the starting quarterback as of yet, although it will either be Marcus Stokes or Air Noland (or perhaps both).

For UNLV, Dan Mullen is going to employ a fascinating two-QB plan to start the season using two familiar faces. Former Oklahoma QB Jackson Arnold and Alex Orji, formerly Michigan's starter, will each play a part.

Given the duality of both, it's an intriguing combination. And given Mullen's success with quarterbacks, one can't help but wonder what he can draw out of Arnold that others couldn't.

As for this game, it seems like a tough spot for a new head coach. UNLV delivered another 10-win season last year, and it's poised to start off the year on a positive note.

We're laying the points. In Mullen we trust.

articles.title: Pierre Sage: Crystal Palace head coach on Everton loss, facing Man City and how his career prepared him for the Premier League
articles.summary: Pierre Sage has drawn comparisons to former Crystal Palace boss Oliver Glasner after his success at Lens; however, he lost his first Premier League game to Everton; watch Crystal Palace vs Man City on Friday Night Football from 7pm live on Sky Sports; kick-off 8pm
articles.body:
When asked if he enjoyed his first experience of the world's most famous league, his first response is 'we lost' - showing how seriously he is taking not only the result, but the job as a whole.

"I'm not here in an attraction park, you can say that. I'm here to win games, the job is like this and I'm not happy to lose this game," was his follow up when speaking to Sky Sports ahead of Friday's match against Manchester City.

"I understood with this game that we are able to do things and it's difficult when you know you are able to do it and you don't do it for the duration of the game," Sage continued. "That's why I was a little bit frustrated because we played well during the first half and it's not normal that we played as we did in the second half.

"That's why we need to be more consistent. We need to work a lot, we need to understand together better. We need to be fluent, to be smooth in our play and the only thing to do is to work."

The focus on winning is no surprise for a manager who achieved incredible things with Lens last season. They finished second in Ligue 1 behind PSG - ahead of the likes of Marseille and Lyon - securing a place in the Champions League. They also won their first Coupe de France title.

In fact, it's the striking similarities to Oliver Glasner that saw Sage appointed at Crystal Palace on a three-year deal. These have been evident too in the games the Frenchman has managed so far.

"I think that's why the club chose me because we [himself and Glanser] are in line in a lot of principles, but we are different for the moment," Sage said.

"He won and I didn't win here yet, but the most important thing for me is not to be in line with that. It's to be consistent with the previous manager, but in my way.

"When I left France, people said when I left that I was leaving Champions League football to only play in the Europa League and I told them I'd be playing in the Champions League every weekend."

Crystal Palace represents another step in Sage's varied career that has seen him do everything from technical director to academy coach. But it is his time as an assistant that prepared him most for life as a Premier League boss.

"When I was an assistant, I understood the training process, but I also understood how to manage the guys," he explained.

"It's not only with the Premier League, it's like this in every country, but to understand the Premier League, the most important thing I did was to watch a lot of games.

"I like to be in contact with all the departments because I consider everybody important in a club and if we have success, it's all together and when we lose, it's the same. That's why it's important to be connected to all these people and to understand their job."

It will take a team effort on Friday Night Football when Crystal Palace will host Man City - Sage's first Premier League game at Selhurst Park.

"Everybody has told me it [the atmosphere at Selhurst Park] is incredible, it's really different to the other clubs and I'm happy to discover that," the Frenchman said.

"But the most important thing is the play and the result and if we can make them [the fans] happy at the end of the game, it will be a good satisfaction.

"It will be a difficult game because there's a lot of talent in their squad. When you have a new manager, there's a lot of energy at the beginning because you don't really know who will be the starter. That's why it's important to be at our best level for this game."

articles.title: Yaya Toure becomes first African coach to lead a team into Champions League
articles.summary: Ivory Coast legend Toure takes Slovan Bratislava into the group phase two months after joining the Slovakian club.
articles.body:
Legendary former Ivory Coast footballer Yaya Toure has made history by becoming the first African coach to lead a team into the main round of the UEFA Champions League with his club Slovan Bratislava.

The Slovakian club secured a place in the European club competition on Wednesday after winning their two-legged tie against NK Celje with a 3-2 aggregate score in Slovenia.

Toure joined the club as its head coach in June and has made a quick impression, leading the Slovak champions to four wins in the league and ensuring a spot in the biggest club competition in the world.

Slovan Bratislava began their qualifying round for the Champions League in July with a 2-0 win over Georgian team Saburtalo before drawing the second leg of the tie 1-1.

They then beat Sweden’s Mjallby in both legs of their second qualifying round to secure a place in the playoffs, where they overcame the Slovenian club over two legs to enter the main round.

Toure, who is counted amongst the greatest African footballers of all time, was serenaded with a rendition of the “Yaya Toure” chant made popular during his time as a key member of a successful Manchester City team of the 2010s.

The 43-year-old retired as a player in 2019, following a trophy-laden 18-year career as a midfielder in top European leagues. Prior to joining City in 2010, he played for Spanish giants Barcelona, where he won the Champions League (2008-09), two La Liga titles (2008-09 and 2009-10), the Spanish Super Cup (2008-09), the UEFA Super Cup (2009-10) and the FIFA Club World Cup (2010). He then went on to win three Premier League titles, one FA Cup and three English League Cups with City.

Toure is the joint most decorated African footballer, having won four African Footballer of the Year awards from 2011 to 2014. He won the Africa Cup of Nations with The Elephants in 2015.

Prior to joining the Slovakian club as the manager, Toure worked as assistant manager in several clubs across Europe – from Leyton Orient in the United Kingdom to Belgium – before joining his former Manchester City manager as assistant coach of the Saudi Arabian national team in 2023.

Toure’s club Slovan Bratislava will learn their Champions League fate late on Thursday, when the group phase draw will be held in Madrid.

articles.title: Kim Min-su: Rangers bolster wing options with signing of Girona winger
articles.summary: Rangers sign South Korean winger Kim Min-su, who admits he was surprised to learn of the club's interest in recruiting him from Girona.
articles.body:
Rangers have bolstered their wide options with the arrival of Kim Min-su from Girona for an undisclosed fee, with manager Derek McInnes saying the South Korean adds "another exciting dimension to the squad".

The 20-year-old has signed a four-year contract, with the option of a further year, becoming Rangers' 12th signing of the summer.

Kim was loaned to second-tier Andorra last term and leaves Girona after their relegation from La Liga. He scored 19 goals in 84 appearances for Girona B and played eight times for their senior team. At Andorra, he netted six times in 40 games and provided four assists.

And he admits "it was a surprise" to hear of Rangers' interest.

Raskin nears Rangers exit after missing Czech trip

Play to win in Jablonec, McInnes tells Rangers

"I have a lot of confidence in myself to come here," he told club media.

"I am an attacking player and I make many chances. I am direct and score goals – this is the most important thing.

"I'm here to win titles and to become a winner with Rangers. I want to help the team to be better every day, to be a good person and to do everything I can to help the team win everything that comes our way.

"I have a lot of excitement and I believe I have the mentality of a winner. I want to face whatever comes next head-on and I'm going to give the club what it deserves."

The Ibrox outfit have been chasing new wingers, with Minsu joining Djeidi Gassama, Findlay Curtis and Ross McCausland, as well as another summer recruit in Daisuke Yokota.

Rangers had been poised to buy PSV Eindhoven's Couhaib Driouech earlier this month, but the 24-year-old had been carrying a minor injury.

Brighton then rejected a £7.5m offer from Ibrox for Amario Cozier-Duberry, 21.

"Strengthening our options in the forward areas has been a real target and focus for us throughout this window and we believe he will add another exciting dimension to the squad," manager Derek McInnes said of his new winger, who will wear the 10 jersey.

"Minsu is a talented young player with excellent technical ability, energy and a real desire to develop and we are looking forward to working with him."

articles.title: Nicolas Jackson transfer to Aston Villa: Why striker from Chelsea could yet prove to be underrated
articles.summary: With Nicolas Jackson set for a move to Aston Villa, Adam Bate looks at why the criticism of the Chelsea striker's finishing overlooks his greatest asset and why his old boss Unai Emery could be the man to unlock the player's potential...
articles.body:
The words of Brentford owner Matthew Benham when speaking at the MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference earlier this year feel particularly relevant here. "For a striker, getting in position is way more informative than finishing," Benham explained.

"There is an awful amount of randomness in finishing. For example, if you show me two players at a similar level and they both scored 15 goals last season but one of them had twice the number of chances, I want the guy who had twice the number of chances."

Benham, whose analytical background has underpinned Brentford's overperformance, offered the example of Beto at Everton but these principles also apply to Jackson. "The fact that he is getting in position for the shot, that is really important for us," he added.

When it comes to finding the positions that result in shots, it is no exaggeration to state that there are few better at it than the much-maligned Jackson. Indeed, there is some statistical evidence that puts him among the absolute elite at getting chances to score.

Since the start of the decade, factoring in everyone who has played at least 5,000 Premier League minutes, and excluding penalties, there is only Erling Haaland with a higher expected-goals figure per 90 minutes than Jackson. He is a chance magnet.

Although Jackson reached double figures for Premier League goals in both of his seasons as a Chelsea player, the problem was putting those chances away. He was able to convert only 18 of his 61 - sixty-one - big chances as a Premier League player.

It was a return that compared unfavourably to the best finishers in the competition and eventually convinced Chelsea to look elsewhere. Jackson's season on loan at Bayern Munich saw some of the patterns repeat. He continued to get into excellent positions.

In fact, his goal return was impressive enough for Bayern. He scored 11 goals in all competitions but was starved of minutes, starting only 15 matches. In terms of goals from open play in the Bundesliga, only Harry Kane had a better record per 90 minutes.

Perhaps that is not such a surprise given Bayern's utter dominance in Germany but the marginal difference between the eventual winner of the European Golden Shoe and Jackson is interesting. Kane averaged 0.79 open-play goals per 90 to Jackson's 0.72.

Criticism still follows him but Bayern coach Vincent Kompany is an admirer. "I have to say that I have noticed since I have been here that when everything is going well in the team, there are attempts to single out a player or two without any reason," he said.

"The guy has not done anything wrong, he trained extremely well, he won the AFCON, but there are always stories about a player or two." He added: "When Harry Kane plays in your position, or Michael Olise, or Luis Díaz, it is a bit difficult. There is nothing more."

Kompany knows that Jackson did his job and he did it well. Towards the end of the season, when Bayern's focus switched to Europe, he scored in three consecutive Bundesliga games. Speaking to Sky, Bayern legend Lothar Matthaus laid it all out.

"Kompany is convinced of Jackson's abilities and would have liked to keep him in Munich. But he is too expensive. Kompany has made it clear internally that he would like to keep Jackson, but obviously at a certain price that Chelsea might not accept."

For Aston Villa, who received a British record transfer fee of £117m from Chelsea for Morgan Rogers, the circumstances are different. And Unai Emery has good reason to believe that he could coax more than anyone else from this particular player.

It was working with Emery at Villarreal that opened up these career opportunities for Jackson. And there is no need to take anyone else's word for that. Speaking to Sky Sports about this, Jackson was emphatic. "Unai taught me everything about football."

He added: "When I was from Senegal, I knew how to play but I did not understand how to run on the pitch. I was just running like crazy, taking the ball and just dribbling, making my own stuff. He changed all that and made me into a different kind of player."

It was Jackson who scored the final goal of Emery's highly successful reign at Villarreal. He netted the late winner at home to Almeria on what was an emotional occasion for the club following the passing of their popular vice-president José Manuel Llaneza.

What were Emery's farewell words about Jackson in the press conference afterwards before his move to Villa was confirmed? "He has to evolve so that his work for the team can be transformed into effectiveness." Clearly, that evolution is not yet complete.

But Jackson only turned 25 years old in June. For comparison, Ollie Watkins has already turned 30. Tammy Abraham, who spent time on loan at Villa last season, is 28. There is more to come. Lots to work with. And every reason to believe that Emery can help.

articles.title: Iñigo: “Veo la Champions desde niño y me ilusiona mucho”
articles.standfirst: El técnico, pendiente del sorteo europeo, debutará esta temporada en la máxima competición continental
articles.summary: El técnico, pendiente del sorteo europeo, debutará esta temporada en la máxima competición continental
articles.body: Iñigo Pérez espera con ilusión el sorteo de Liga de Campeones que vivirá por primera vez esta tarde como parte implicada. El técnico del Villarreal espera que su equipo de la cara toda vez que analiza también la llegada de Nathan Saliba, último fichaje amarillo Estado de la plantilla / Fichaje: “El equipo está bien. No tenemos bajas. Contento, porque es un mérito bien atribuido al preparador físico, pero también es en parte por los jugadores que se cuidan. Contento por Nathan, es un jugador que nos aporta algo que quizás nos falta o tenemos en pequeñas dosis. Espero que sea fácil su adaptación, pero habrá que ir viendo cómo se encuentra” Reforzar posición en el medio: “Es una posición que demanda todo. Generar juego, ser capaz de ser el motor y marcan la altura del equipo. Estábamos muy bien cubiertos, pero hoy veremos quién nos toca en Champions y eso son demandas de volumen importantes. Si queríamos mantener el nivel de excelencia, era importante incorporar” Ganas de ganar: “Siempre hay ganas de ganar, es adictivo y quiero sumar ya la primera victoria con este grupo, y quiero que sea mañana” Arranque liga: “No sé si las puntuaciones a estas alturas de la temporada son buenas o malas, las temporadas son largas como pare tener paciencia y ver los rangos adecuados. Venimos de dos partidos de liga en un ascenso, debemos mantener ese proceso y ojalá eso se transforme en puntaje y reforzar la autoestima por el trabajo hecho” Pocos cambios: “Soy un entrenador que le gusta utilizar a todos sus jugadores, siempre y cuando haya podido ver en ellos la capacidad para responder a el partido. Veo que todo el mundo está capacitado, se refrenda en cada entrenamiento y están con ganas de participar. Cuando el volumen de partidos aumente, veremos cambios y combinaciones” Segundo equipo que más chuta: “Son preguntas reiterativas del año pasado con el Rayo, donde nos pasó lo mismo. El porcentaje de acierto está siendo escaso, pero prefiero tener ese tipo de disposición y creo que a la larga el nivel de jugadores se impondrá. Me preocuparía más si en dos partidos no hubiésemos chutado y la sensación e peligro fuera nula” Sobre el partido en Mendizorroza: “Siempre hablo de frecuencia emocional o ambiental y es parecido al de Santander, con aficiones muy involucradas. Un juego específico, más directo, más vertical, que, si no igualas, te sientes acosado y con vértigo. Igualar la frecuencia emocional y luego imponerte en el juego. Aprendimos la lección en Santander” Sobre Mikautadze: “Lo de que no espere solo en última línea, debe mantenerlo. Soy optimista de que pueda generar juego. Con el cambio de altura que vimos en el Metropolitano, puede añadir registros y no ser tan localizable para el rival” Como les han afectado los horarios: “El otro día el ejemplo de Santi, y de Koke en el rival, son dos ejemplos de jugadores que no paran, vimos como les afectó . Las condiciones atmosféricas son exigentes y te hacen tomar decisiones. También es inicio de temporada, cuando la condición física no es la más puntera. No planteas el partido en torno a esto, pero sí que hay que tenerlo en cuenta” Sorteo Champions: "Soy sincero y me hace mucha ilusión participar en la Champions. Es un torneo que ves desde que eres niño y todo el mundo de lo que sucede el martes y los miércoles. Estar aquí en este nuevo proyecto es muy motivador para mí. No tengo un viaje especial, pero si tenemos suerte con los viajes, es positivo. Pero con pertenecer al Villarreal y estar en este sorteo, estoy orgulloso" Sabe que tendrá rivales fuertes: “Sabiendo que además te va a pasar, es una torpeza seguir evitándolo en tu cabeza. Te va a tocar alguno de los gordos. Debemos ilusionarnos con ir a los mejores campos, ante los mejores jugadores e ir a ganar. Plantearlo de un modo atrevido y organizado. En la liga española estamos acostumbrados a jugar contra los mejores, por qué no hacerlo en otros países”

articles.title: Andy Burnham has a lot of Irish roots - will he play on them during his visit?
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham was quick to talk up his proud Irish roots on his last visit to Northern Ireland and we can expect more of the same this time.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham was quick to talk up his proud Irish roots on his last visit to Northern Ireland and we can expect more of the same this time.

Back then, the Mayor of Manchester was still plotting his route to Westminister when he addressed the Alliance Party conference in March.

"If only my ancestors who left Drogheda for Liverpool in the late 1800s could see me now," he told delegates in Belfast before going on to say: "It's nice to feel wanted by a political party."

That was a pointed dig at the then Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer who was trying to block Burnham's pathway to No 10.

Much has changed in the six months since then.

Now Burnham is back in Northern Ireland as prime minister and expect his Irish heritage to feature once more.

He may mention that his father Roy is a Protestant and his mother Eileen is Catholic.

A former altar boy, Burnham has said his Catholic upbringing had a big impact on his life.

In fact, he once said his three biggest influences growing up were Everton Football Club, Labour and the Catholic Church.

His Irish roots on his mother's side also helped shape his political outlook.

He has often talked about his great-grandfather Edmund "Ned" Burke who lived in Drogheda before emigrating with his family to Liverpool in the late 19th Century.

Like so many who made the same journey, he worked in the docks and was deeply involved in Liverpool's Irish Catholic community.

He also fought in World War One after joining the King's Liverpool Regiment but was captured by the Germans just months after being deployed to the front line.

He spent two years in captivity before he died at the age of 34 in 1918 shortly before the end of the war.

In a speech ahead of the Brexit referendum in 2016, Burnham recalled his great-grandfather's sacrifice and said he would have urged them to learn the lessons of the past.

"Breaking away from any group is always a recipe for confrontation and conflict," he said

He added the best way to honour his great-grandfather was to carry on fighting for "a more united and less nationalistic Europe".

Away from this family links he has also been greatly influenced by Irish musicians such as the Pogues, Christy Moore and the Undertones.

He has even played guitar as former Undertones front man Feargal Sharkey performed their greatest hit, Teenage Kicks.

During his time as mayor of Manchester, Burnham worked closely with the Irish diaspora and attended many cultural events.

He also visited Dublin many times meeting the then President Michael Higgins and other leading politicians as he sought to improve Anglo-Irish relations post Brexit.

But Burnham will also be well aware of the political pit falls when questioned about such sensitive topics as Irish reunification and a border poll.

Expect him to sidestep such tricky questions and instead talk up the importance of building relationships and respecting the Good Friday Agreement.

But he may find it harder to avoid questions about providing more financial support for the Stormont Executive and he will be reminded of something else he told delegates at the Alliance conference.

That all the nations and regions should get the maximum level of devolved funding from Westminster to achieve growth and deliver better living standards for their people.

But that was message delivered by Andy Burnham the political outcast and not by Andy Burnham the prime minister.

articles.title: World Cup 2034 hosts Saudi Arabia back Infantino amid FIFA crisis
articles.summary: Saudi football federation says it supports Infantino’s ’efforts’ as he garners support to remain in power as president.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia, hosts of the World Cup 2034, have thrown their ⁠⁠support behind ⁠⁠embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino as he continues to face criticism over the collapse of the governing body’s controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise ⁠⁠proposal.

In a statement released on Thursday, the Saudi Arabian Football Federation (SAFF) welcomed FIFA’s acknowledgement of mistakes, its apology and the decision to scrap the proposal, while calling for direct dialogue ⁠⁠among football’s stakeholders to restore unity.

“At this time, SAFF supports the continued efforts of FIFA President Gianni Infantino and FIFA’s leadership to restore unity across the football family and continue growing the game for the benefit of all,” the federation said.

Saudi Arabia’s backing is significant given its expanding role in world football.

The kingdom’s Public Investment Fund partnered with FIFA for the 2025 Club World Cup and was also an official supporter in North America and Asia of this year’s World Cup, underscoring the kingdom’s growing ties with the global governing body.

“The past three editions of the FIFA World Cup have ⁠⁠demonstrated what football can achieve when its global family works ⁠⁠together,” the federation said in a statement.

“The FIFA President’s contribution to growing the game worldwide over almost a decade should also be recognised.”

SAFF urged FIFA leaders to hold “direct face-to-face dialogue … with all concerns addressed openly”.

Infantino has not called a meeting of his 37-member FIFA Council, which includes Saudi official Yasser Al Misehal, and instead met with most of his FIFA management team in Rabat, Morocco, three weeks ago.

The FIFA president is up for re-election for a fourth term next March. He has been ⁠⁠widely criticised since tabling a now abandoned proposal to sell off a 20 percent stake in a commercial body for FIFA tournament ⁠⁠rights, with several countries withdrawing their support for ⁠⁠his candidacy.

The Swiss-Italian administrator is under pressure from three confederations to resign, including UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America and the Caribbean.

The regional governing bodies have ‌‌discussed a potential vote of no confidence in Infantino.

Infantino, ‌‌who ‌‌retains support from the African and South American confederations, has sought to sideline the confederations and appeal directly to individual members.

Italy became the latest national federation to withdraw its support, saying its decision was “intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC’s position… regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions”.

However, European football body UEFA, which had threatened to pull out of the FIFA Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland next month, said it would formally withdraw its threat to boycott FIFA competitions after receiving assurances that Infantino’s failed sell-off plan will not be revived.
