articles.title: Week 1 What to Watch: UNC looks for revenge against TCU, NC State-Virginia open with ACC matchup
articles.summary: This year's Week 1 slate features eight FBS games and several compelling storylines to kick off the year.
articles.body:
The offseason is over, and college football is back … for a few teams, at least.

Even with an eight-game slate on tap for Saturday, Aug. 29, there is still plenty to look for as the college football season begins.

The day begins as North Carolina takes on TCU in Dublin, Ireland. This will be the official start of Year 2 in the Bill Belichick era at UNC, and he will be looking to improve on the disappointing 4-8 2025 campaign that included a 48-14 blowout loss to TCU in the season opener.

Saturday's slate concludes as Memphis heads west to take on UNLV. Charles Huff will debut as the Tigers' new head coach after going 7-5 with Southern Miss last season. The Rebels are not only preseason favorites in the Mountain West, but also many analysts' choice to get the Group of Six College Football Playoff spot.

Here are the five biggest games in Week 1:

UNC overhauled its quarterback room this offseason. Last year, Max Johnson played in four games while Gio Lopez saw action in 11 games. Johnson is now the starting quarterback at Georgia Southern, while Lopez stayed in the ACC and took his talents to Wake Forest.

The Tar Heels have named Billy Edwards Jr. as their starting quarterback . Edwards began his collegiate career at Maryland, spending three seasons with the Terrapins. He transferred to Wisconsin last season, but played in only two games after dealing with a knee injury.

The Horned Frogs blew out UNC in Week 1 last year and finished the season with an overall 9-4 record, but they went 5-4 in Big 12 play. It did mark back-to-back nine-win seasons for head coach Sonny Dykes, and the Horned Frogs have won at least nine games in three of the four seasons he has been at the helm. They need a strong start to the year and would love to go into the Oct. 3 matchup against BYU with a 4-0 record and momentum.

TCU will be led by Harvard transfer quarterback Jaden Craig after Josh Hoover left for Indiana in the offseason. Craig is more of a pocket passer and threw for 2,869 yards, 25 touchdowns and 7 interceptions last season as the Crimson finished 9-2 in their FCS season.

One preseason AP-ranked team will see action in Week 1 as the No. 14 Trojans host San Jose State. USC is coming off a 9-4 season in its second year in the Big Ten. The Trojans are still searching for their first College Football Playoff berth with Lincoln Riley as their head coach.

Jayden Maiava played in all 13 games for USC last season. He finished with 3,711 passing yards, 24 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. The QB doesn't rush often, but did tally six rushing touchdowns.

USC's big question will be who steps up at wide receiver after the departure of Makai Lemon (drafted 20th overall by the Philadelphia Eagles ) and Ja'Kobi Lane (third-round pick by the Baltimore Ravens ). The teammates combined for 1,901 yards and 15 touchdowns last season.

San Jose State had a disappointing 3-9 season last year with a 2-6 record in the Mountain West. The Spartans named transfer quarterback Luke Weaver as their starter against USC. Weaver played in just five games at Hawaii last year and finished with 628 passing yards, 6 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. He won the job over redshirt freshman Robert McDaniel and true freshman Daniel Rolovich.

There are only two Week 1 matchups between conference opponents, and NC State facing Virginia is easily the bigger one.

The Wolfpack finished last season 8-5 after beating Memphis in the Gasparilla Bowl. NC State will have a familiar face under center as CJ Bailey is back for his third year as the starter.

So far, over two years, he has tallied 5,518 passing yards, 42 passing touchdowns, 19 interceptions, 494 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns in 25 games. One thing to watch here is the Wolfpack's running game. Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas, and redshirt sophomore Jayden Scott is expected to take over in the backfield.

Virginia made it all the way to the ACC championship last season. The Cavaliers fell to Duke 27-20 in overtime, but picked up a win in the Gator Bowl to finish 11-3 — their most wins in program history .

UVA will start transfer QB Beau Pribula in Week 1; he played in 10 games for Missouri last season. Pribula threw for 1,941 yards with 11 touchdowns and 9 interceptions. He also ran for 297 yards and six more touchdowns on the ground.

The Seminoles will open their 2026 season at home against New Mexico State in a non-conference matchup. Florida State is looking to rebound after a disappointing 5-7 finish last year. The Noles only managed two conference wins, beating Wake Forest and Clemson.

Former FSU quarterback Tommy Castellanos is in the transfer portal; the Seminoles will be led by transfer QB Ashton Daniels. After spending three years at Stanford, Daniels transferred to Auburn last year. He played in only four games and finished with just 797 passing yards, 3 touchdowns and 2 interceptions.

Mike Norvell has been Florida State's head coach for six seasons. The team has gone 38-34 in that span, and he enters this year firmly on the hot seat .

New Mexico State started last season 3-2, but then lost five consecutive games. When the dust settled, the Aggies finished the year 4-8 and went 2-6 in Conference USA play. New Mexico State will turn to Trey Hedden as its starting quarterback. Hedden transferred to the Aggies from Furman. Last year, he had 2,967 yards, 17 touchdowns and 13 interceptions for the Paladins.

After back-to-back 10+ win seasons under Ryan Silverfield, the Tigers took a step back last season, finishing 8-5 and going 4-4 in conference play. Silverfield left for Arkansas, and now Huff begins a new era at Memphis.

The Tigers have had a lengthy quarterback battle between Marcus Stokes and former five-star QB Air Noland . Stokes transferred to Memphis from West Florida (Division II). Noland spent one season with Ohio State and last season with South Carolina. He's appeared in just two games and is 2-of-3 passing for 13 yards.

UNLV is a popular pick to make the CFP as the Group of Six representative. Part of that stems from belief in Dan Mullen's system after his team finished 10-4 last year.

The Rebels also have an ongoing quarterback battle between Jackson Arnold (who transferred in from Auburn) and Alex Orji, a former Michigan QB who played in three games for UNLV last season before suffering season-ending injuries. Arnold played in 10 games for Auburn last year before being benched for poor performance. He finished with 1,309 yards, 6 touchdowns and 2 interceptions.

articles.title: 3 things to know about the SEC, which could overwhelm the 12-team playoff field this season
articles.summary: Not a single SEC team received a first-place vote in the preseason AP Top 25.
articles.body:
How many SEC teams will make the College Football Playoff ?

As teams from the Big Ten have won each of the first two 12-team playoffs, the SEC has gotten eight teams in the field in that span. That's the most of any league.

But how much are playoff bids worth when someone else is winning the title?

It's a question that looms large over a league that appears to once again have a lot of teams capable of making the playoff but few that could actually win it.

Here's what you need to know about the SEC ahead of the 2026 college football season.

Who are the legitimate national title contenders?

With just a week to go until the season begins in earnest, Texas is the only SEC team among the top five betting favorites for the national title. And given how popular Texas is among public bettors, that popularity is likely priced into the Longhorns ' +650 odds alongside Notre Dame and behind Ohio State at +600.

Throw in the fact that no one among the AP poll's 69 voters put an SEC team No. 1 on his or her ballot and the SEC is in a unique spot this season. There appear to be a lot of really, really good teams in the conference. But how many of them are capable of winning the national title?

You'll notice in the table above that Texas isn't even the favorite to win the conference. That honor goes to Georgia, with odds just slightly better than the Longhorns. The Bulldogs are 3-0 against the Longhorns over the past two seasons and the two teams do not meet in the regular season in 2026 for the first time since Texas' arrival in the conference.

Georgia could have its best team since the one that went 13-1 in 2023. The Bulldogs are largely homegrown and are looking to get the run game really humming again after a relatively lackluster last two seasons. QB Gunner Stockton is a borderline Heisman favorite, though replacing Zachariah Branch 's production at wide receiver will be imperative for his chances at the award.

Knowing this could be Arch Manning 's final season in Austin, Texas made a bunch of impact moves in the transfer portal. The Longhorns added star Auburn WR Cam Coleman (Auburn) along with RBs Raleek Brown ( Arizona State ) and Hollywood Smothers (NC State). Texas also appeared to dodge a big injury bullet last week when left tackle Trevor Goosby's knee injury was diagnosed as a bone bruise and his recovery timeline put him on track to potentially be available against Ohio State in Week 2.

The SEC looks to be the hardest conference to figure out at the top. Even though no team got a first-place vote, the league has seven in the top 13 of the AP poll. And all seven of those teams have odds to win the league of 12-1 or better.

Good luck trying to pick the exact finishing order of the top half of the conference.

There's a strong case to be made for any of those seven teams' conference championship and playoff hopes too. LSU? The last time QB Sam Leavitt was healthy, he was helping lead Arizona State to the CFP. The offensive line in front of him should be solid thanks to the addition of Jordan Seaton , and the receiving options will be plentiful if Florida transfer Eugene Wilson III can stay healthy. Yes, there's that huge trip to Ole Miss for Lane Kiffin's squad, but the Tigers get Texas A&M, Alabama and Texas all at home.

The Rebels still have QB Trinidad Chambliss and RB Kewan Lacy on offense and head coach Pete Golding added a lot to the defense via the transfer portal. Getting Texas and Oklahoma on the road is tough, but at least the Georgia game is at home.

Texas A&M is fresh off its first playoff appearance and brings back QB Marcel Reed and WR Mario Craver . The Aggies held opposing QBs to just 177 passing yards a game in 2025 and should have a very strong pass defense again this season even while having to replace Cashius Howell and his 11.5 sacks.

After a long summer camp battle, Alabama named Keelon Russell the starter after Ty Simpson 's departure to the NFL. A bounce-back season from Ryan Coleman-Williams will go a long way to putting the Crimson Tide closer to the category of national title contenders, especially if head coach Kalen DeBoer and offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb can figure out what the heck was going on with the team's running game in 2025.

Oklahoma also has dreams of back-to-back playoff appearances, especially with a win at Michigan in Week 2. The Sooners have one of the toughest schedules among SEC contenders. OU has to travel to Georgia, Florida and Missouri, plays Texas in Dallas and gets Ole Miss, Texas A&M at home. A 9-3 record might not be enough to make the SEC title game, but it could be enough for a spot in the CFP.

Who is in for a surprise season in 2026?

Now that we've established that the SEC's crowd of contenders is tightly packed, it's also likely that someone outside of that group will finish near the top of the standings.

Just look at the last three seasons of the preseason media poll. In the conference's last year with divisions in 2023, Missouri was picked to finish fifth in the East. The Tigers went 6-2 in SEC play and finished 11-2 overall after winning the Cotton Bowl. In 2024, South Carolina was picked to finish 13th in the league after the additions of Oklahoma and Texas. The Gamecocks went 5-3 in SEC play in a massive tie for fourth.

Last summer, Vanderbilt occupied that No. 13 spot in the preseason poll. The Commodores became one of the best stories of the season and finished a game out of a tie for first place in the league as Diego Pavia was second in the Heisman voting to Fernando Mendoza .

If there's something about starting the season at No. 13, then Vanderbilt is in for another big year. The Commodores were picked in that spot again at SEC media days in July. Pavia is gone, but transfer QB Blaze Berlowitz takes over after beating out five-star freshman Jared Curtis for the starting job. We will know a lot about Vandy over the first five weeks of the season. From Weeks 3-5, Vanderbilt plays NC State and visits Auburn and Georgia.

Auburn was picked 12th in the conference and could be primed for a first-year bounce under new coach Alex Golesh. The former USF coach brought along ex-Bulls QB Byrum Brown after Brown threw for over 3,000 and rushed for over 1,000 yards in 2025. Did you know Auburn hasn't had a winning season since 2020?

The Gamecocks could also surprise, though injuries to OT Jacarrius Peak and edge rusher Dylan Stewart are a concern. The two have been out for fall camp and coach Shane Beamer said both won't be ready for the start of the season. Stewart has 11 sacks over his first two seasons in Columbia. Peak, a transfer from NC State, is being counted on to bolster an offensive line that struggled mightily at times in 2025. Better line play will go a long way for LaNorris Sellers to live up to the NFL Draft hype that preceded his disappointing 2025 season.

articles.title: UEFA Prepares Criminal Complaint in Swiss Courts Against FIFA's Infantino over World Cup Sell-Off
articles.summary: MONACO (AP) — UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Swiss courts for possible financial mismanagement over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.
articles.body:
MONACO (AP) — UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Swiss courts for possible financial mismanagement over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.

The governing body of European soccer announced its intentions in court documents filed Thursday in the U.S. seeking access to possible evidence related to the sell-off plan, which was withdrawn after a furious backlash by UEFA and other global soccer leaders.

The move increases the pressure on Infantino, who is facing the biggest crisis in his 10 years as FIFA's leader.

UEFA filed documents in a Manhattan court requesting discovery of potential evidence from the New York investment fund, Thrive Capital Management, founded by Josh Kushner — the younger brother of President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

UEFA also filed a request in a southern Florida district for authorization of discovery "in a foreign proceeding" against FIFA itself, which has offices in the Miami suburb of Coral Gables.

Under the plan revealed in late July, Thrive and Kushner were to be the anchor investors intending to pay FIFA $4.2 billion for a 20% stake in a subsidiary that would run the soccer body's commercial events, including the World Cup.

"UEFA and its counsel are contemplating a Swiss criminal proceeding against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials for criminal mismanagement under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code," UEFA's lawyers state in a 56-page document seen by The Associated Press.

The document suggests the $4.2 billion figure could be a "fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit."

FIFA is expected to have about $5 billion in cash reserves after the World Cup in North America boosted its revenue to a record $15 billion over the 2023-26 commercial cycle.

"The question is therefore why the FIFA president believed he needed outside investors to expand development funding," UEFA said in a statement.

Infantino dropped the sell-off plan on Aug. 1 after intense criticism led by soccer officials in Europe.

UEFA had warned against destroying potential evidence

UEFA first threatened to take legal action on Aug. 3 when it warned FIFA against destroying or hiding any "relevant materials" related to the plan. Thursday's legal move was revealed to its member federations in Monaco just two hours before the Champions League draw began.

"Infantino claimed that the plan would 'unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that FIFA has,'" UEFA lawyers told the courts. "In truth, it was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA's most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family.

"Under the terms Infantino announced, those investors stood to acquire a permanent financial interest in FIFA's commercial arm for $4.2 billion, implying an absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20 billion, a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer."

Thrive declined to comment. FIFA was approached for comment.

Swiss prosecutors' poor results in FIFA trials

It was unclear if UEFA would send a potential criminal complaint to the Swiss federal prosecution office in Bern or to local prosecutors in FIFA's home city Zurich.

The Swiss attorney general's office has a poor record in recent years prosecuting cases of alleged corruption linked to FIFA and soccer officials.

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter, former UEFA president Michel Platini and the influential Qatari president of Champions League title holder Paris Saint-Germain, Nasser al-Khelaïfi , all were acquitted twice at trials in Switzerland.

The crisis has raised questions about Infantino's future. Just months ago, he was widely expected to win another four-year term in the FIFA election set for March 2027, but a growing number of soccer federations around the world but mainly in Europe have withdrawn their support , with some joining UEFA in calling on him to step down , ideally before the Nov. 18 deadline for candidates.

"Should the current FIFA president nevertheless seek another mandate, UEFA will join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that member associations are offered a credible alternative," the European body said, "one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change."

articles.title: Julian Alvarez transfer news: Arsenal only likely exit after Atletico say no to Barcelona
articles.summary: Julian Alvarez has not attended Atletico Madrid training since being told privately that the club would not sell him to Barcelona.
articles.body:
Julian Alvarez has not attended Atletico Madrid training since being told privately the club would not sell him to Barcelona and it appears the striker's only way out is with a move to Arsenal .

Sources told BBC Sport that Atletico communicated privately to Alvarez and his advisers earlier this week that they will not negotiate with the Catalan club over a move for the Argentina international.

The 26-year-old has since missed two consecutive days of training citing illness.

The La Liga club also released two public statements in the space of 24 hours reiterating their stance that Alvarez will not be granted his wish to join Barca in the coming days.

Atletico, however, are open to selling Alvarez to Arsenal and have held direct talks with the Premier League champions over what would be one of the biggest transfers of the summer.

Atleti director Mateu Alemany was in London last week, where he is understood to have met with Arsenal counterparts - and made clear his side would seek a fee of 150m euros (£128m).

Mikel Arteta is desperate to sign Alvarez this month but his steadfast desire to join Barcelona has seen Arsenal 's pursuit halted.

However, it is understood discussions between Atletico and Arsenal over a club-to-club agreement for Alvarez have been positive.

Indeed, in the event of Alvarez giving Arsenal the green light to proceed with his signing in the coming days, a deal should move quickly.

On Wednesday, in response to comments from Barcelona president Joan Laporte in which he insisted they still wanted to sign Alvarez, Atletico released a statement that read : "There is 0% chance of selling him to Barca."

The Atletico board doubled down on their stance on Thursday, releasing their own statement that read: "The members of Atletico de Madrid's board of directors have unanimously expressed their absolute support for the club's decision to not negotiate the transfer of Julian Alvarez to FC Barcelona."

articles.title: Emiliano Martinez transfer news: Chelsea agree £7.5m deal to sign Aston Villa's World Cup winning goalkeeper
articles.summary: Chelsea agree transfer to sign Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez in deal worth £7.5m; 2022 World Cup winner has been relegated to second choice at Villa Park after arrival of Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki from Parma
articles.body:
Sky Sports News reported Chelsea were considering a late move for Martinez after current No 1 Robert Sanchez came under criticism after his error in Monday's win at Fulham.

Martinez has needed to find a new club after Villa signed Zion Suzuki from Parma for nearly £30m.

He was the subject of interest from Juventus but they chose to sign Guglielmo Vicario from Spurs.

Question marks will now be raised over whether both Sanchez and Mike Penders will remain at Stamford Bridge for the season.

Penders started Chelsea's Carabao Cup tie with Luton on Thursday night, after Sanchez started v Fulham.

It is debatable whether Chelsea need three No 1s as they are not in Europe, and Penders has just returned from his loan at Strasbourg.

Sanchez was expected to be No 1 again this season but his performances have not always been convincing.

This deal for 33-year-old Martinez comes despite denials that Chelsea have been in the market for an experienced goalkeeper.

The Blues came close to signing Mike Maignan from AC Milan last summer but could not agree a fee.

Merson: Martinez is one of the best goalkeepers in the world

Martinez is available and he can be hard work sometimes. He comes across like that. But he's one of the best goalkeepers in the world.

And if Chelsea want to get back to being one of the best in the world, you've got to have a top goalkeeper.

Robert Sanchez is usually a good shot-stopper. This weekend, or against Arsenal at the Emirates in two weeks' time, he could be mind-blowing. He could make save after save after save and you'll sit there and go: 'Wow.' He could save Chelsea next week.

I don't like picking on goalkeepers because it's a hard job - and you make one mistake for every 50 mistakes the outfield players make with their passing.

But the match against Fulham was another game that he brought the other team back into the game.

articles.title: OSU's Jeremiah Smith Predicts Freshman RB Legend Bey Will Be Future Heisman Trophy Contender
articles.summary: Ohio State star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has high expectations for true freshman running back Legend Bey.
articles.body:
Ohio State star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has high expectations for true freshman running back Legend Bey.

"I think I said this back in spring. I said to Luke Montgomery, I said, 'Before Legend Bey leaves Ohio State, he will be a Heisman finalist, or he'll end up winning it,'" Smith told reporters.

"The things he's been doing in practice have been pretty special," Smith added.

Bey was ranked by 247Sports as the nation's No. 6 athlete prospect after playing quarterback in high school.

Ohio State coach Ryan Day said earlier this month that while Bey is still learning to play at running back the team could already "see what a weapon he'll become for us," per Eleven Warriors' Dan Hope .

Bey will now look to make the jump to both college football and a new position in a running back room led by sophomore Bo Jackson.

articles.body: Leon Goretzka era uno de los pocos 'chollos' que quedaban disponibles en el mercado de agentes libres. Desde Alemania se ha ido informando a lo largo de todo el verano sobre su ofrecimiento a diferentes equipos tras finalizar su contrato con el Bayern. Finalizada su participación con Alemania en la Copa del Mundo, la incertidumbre sobre su futuro fue en aumento con el paso de las semanas. Sin prácticamente opciones para continuar su carrera en la Bundesliga, Italia o España se antojaban como sus posibles destinos. Con Onana lesionado y Tielemans vendido al Manchester United, el fichaje de Joao Gomes -expulsado en la primera jornada de la Premier contra el Brighton- se quedaba corto para completar la medular del Aston Villa. Palhinha parecía la opción favorita. Pero, tras firmar por Benfica, Roberto Olabe ha movido ficha para cerrar a Goretzka. Será, por tanto, la primera experiencia del centrocampista alemán fuera de la Bundesliga tras pasar por las filas de Bochum, Schalke y un Bayern donde, en 312 partidos, levantó una Champions, siete Bundesligas, tres POKAL, una Supercopa de Europa, tres Supercopas de Alemania y un Mundial de Clubes.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Derrick Henry is officially a boring-value vet — he leads this list for 2026
articles.summary: Having a balanced, productive fantasy football roster means targeting some veterans who are still getting it done.
articles.body:
Sometimes I think fantasy football turns us all into marketing reps. We want an exciting team, a buzzy team, a team we can promote. But it's important to not lose the plot — at the end of the day, all that matters is the points. Flash is nice, but it's a game about numbers.

Hunting for boring-value veterans has been a fantasy staple of mine for a while, both in fantasy baseball and fantasy football. It's important to see this as a part of a balanced fantasy diet, not the complete meal. I wouldn't want any singular roster overflowing with this type of player, but I nonetheless will be tempted when these values show up over and over again at the August draft tables.

He doesn't run, he doesn't draw attention to himself, he's as vanilla as it gets. But Goff knows how to fill the box score — over the last four years, he has the most passing yards and touchdown passes in the league. How does that apply to fantasy production? He's the QB10, QB7, QB6 and QB9 the last four years . I don't see how much changes this season — the Lions have star skill talent, a favorable schedule and a bunch of indoor games. The current draft market is giving you Goff at the QB17 price, an absolute giveaway.

There's plenty of buzz tied to the Green Bay passing game, as Christian Watson, Jayden Reed, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft show up regularly on target lists. It feels like this is the year head coach Matt LaFleur moves away from a platoon system and lets his best talents cook. If any of those guys pop, it will happen because the underrated Love is mixing the ingredients. And heck, we've already seen some proof of concept here, as Love logged a QB5 season back in 2023 . Since then he's been a little unlucky with injuries and the shape of the offense. But with RB Josh Jacobs on the back-nine and ascending talents on the outside, Love is primed for an easy profit season.

Okay, he's a second-round pick, but I need to squeeze Henry into this piece. His draft price is an enormous opportunity. We all know Henry is moving into his age-32 season and we like to trend younger with our running backs. But Henry shows zero sign of slippage. He's been the RB7, RB3, RB8, RB4, RB16 (despite missing two months!), RB2 and RB3 the last seven seasons , and since he joined the Ravens two years back, he's averaging 5.6 yards a carry. I understand the cliff comes calling for everyone eventually, but Henry hasn't lost a step yet.

And even if Henry does show some skills decline this year, the end zone can bail him out. He's spiked 34 times in 34 Baltimore games, and remember: Lamar Jackson rarely runs at the goal line . Henry could have a bad year and still score a dozen or so times in 2026. He's a perfect target if you pick in the middle or late stages of the second round.

Warren has been an underdog his entire career — the Steelers added him as an undrafted free agent — and maybe that's been baked into his ADP. It's clear the team views him as a committee back — Kenneth Gainwell shared time with Warren last year, and this fall it will be Rico Dowdle. But we can still make a profit here. Warren is reliable as a pass-catcher (139 receptions the last three years, and a lovely 83.7% catch rate) and that directly links with veteran QB Aaron Rodgers, who loves to dump short passes to his backs. Let's face it, Rodgers is on that final lap of his career — he has no interest in getting hit.

Warren could easily catch 60 or more balls this year, in addition to handy work as a platoon back. You might draft him as an RB3 or RB4 and see him rise 1-2 slots on your depth chart as the season moves along.

Back in 2024, Robinson picked up the "PPR scam" label in the fantasy streets. That's what happens when you catch 93 passes but they only go for 699 yards. Robinson kept the volume but turned it downfield last year, finishing with a 92-1,014-4 line. His YPC rose from 7.5 to 11.0, a notable jump. This type of player probably needs a specific scheme and coach to stay in business, but no problem for Robinson — Brian Daboll (his former Giants coach) joins him in Tennessee. Robinson's draft price is kept muted by the presence of rookie Carnell Tate, and I understand anyone who's worried about QB Cam Ward. But I'll be shocked if Robinson doesn't lead the Titans in catches. That WR50 tag is an absurd value.

I understand some of the hesitation here, as Jaylen Waddle joins the team and the Broncos also have a bunch of young, ascending receivers. But Sutton is coming off WR10 and WR12 seasons , and he's scored 25 touchdowns in three years. Are we supposed to assume he's completely mothballed? I understand some reluctance, as Sutton enters his age-31 season. But we can't just look at a player like this, scream "Regression!" and drop the mic. Nobody expects Sutotn to repeat last year's WR12 finish, but he can fall an awfully long way and still beat his WR41 tag. Regress and Win , baby.

If you followed the money, you hit on this last year. Johnson received a juicy extension before the 2025 season, then cranked out a 77-889-3 season. Sure, we'd like more touchdowns. But that type of volume is useful in any league with some form of PPR scoring. Kellen Moore turned out to be a smart hire for the Saints, and Tyler Shough did some good things as a rookie. And Johnson will probably be the team's No. 2 target on opening day, given that WR Jordyn Tyson will miss about two months. Johnson's ADP started in the TE19 range and has merely risen to TE16 since the Tyson news. He was the TE10 last year in half-point PPR leagues , and could easily find that area again.

articles.title: Premier League predictions: Chris Sutton v Royal Blood drummer Ben Thatcher - & AI
articles.summary: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on Royal Blood drummer Ben Thatcher, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.
articles.body:
Defending champions Arsenal made an impressive start to the season against newly-promoted Coventry but face a tougher test against Aston Villa on Monday.

But with the number of outgoings at Villa Park, will it be another eye-opener for Unai Emery's men after last week's heavy defeat by Brighton ?

BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton thinks so.

"There's only one winner with this," he said.

" Aston Villa had a slow start last season, they have lost big players and I just think Arsenal are going to run all over teams this season.

"I think they are going to get better and better which is ominous for everybody else."

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers and a variety of guests.

For week two, he takes on drummer Ben Thatcher from rock band Royal Blood.

Royal Blood's latest single, Ten Over Ten, is out now. It is taken from their fifth studio album, Dead Company, which is released in November.

Do you agree with their scores? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competitions.

Ben is a lifelong Brighton fan who is feeling optimistic about the new season despite seeing more star players like striker Danny Welbeck and defender Jan Paul van Hecke leave the club this summer.

"We loved Danny, because he really fitted into our style of play and he had such a great season last year," Ben told BBC Sport.

"We will miss Van Hecke at the back too, but the thing with Brighton is that we always bounce back. We always come through with the players we bring in that I've never heard of, but they get given this chance.

"I just trust in [ Brighton owner] Tony Bloom. He knows better than anyone about these things, because he has done it so many times before.

"He has sold so many world-class players to other clubs and we have nurtured so many great players to replace them.

"So, I don't feel there is any need to worry right now. Just put the trust in the club and see how we get on.

"It's great to be back in Europe [in the Europa Conference League] but with us potentially playing so many more games, I don't expect us to get there again through our league position this time.

"But my hope is that we won't drop into the bottom half of the table. My thinking is that, as long as we finish in the top 10 again and have a good go at Europe, then that's a great season."

Chris Sutton and Ben Thatcher were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

Crystal Palace had a poor start away to Everton and it looks like there's a bit of interest from Liverpool in Ismaila Sarr.

The one thing they can't do before the end of the window is lose all the best players. But I do think they've got a goal in them.

I thought Man City deserved to win. They were a little bit clunky with Mark Guehi playing in midfield - a penny for the thoughts of Mateo Kovacic - but now they've got the youngster Ayyoub Bouaddi, although he'll need a bit of time to adapt.

I don't think this will be a cruise for City, I think they'll be pushed, but I think they'll get over the line. Erling Haaland didn't score last weekend so I expect him to get up to the mark.

Ben's prediction: Palace lost 3-0 to City home and away last season, but I reckon they will nab a goal this time. We are still waiting to see what City are like without Pep Guardiola which makes this harder to call. 1-3

I covered Nottingham Forest against Leeds last weekend and in fairness that was a really tight game. Oliver Glasner's gone into Forest with a big reputation but they went through four managers last year and the owner is notoriously impatient if things don't go well.

They didn't go big in the transfer window but they have got Liam Delap and he'll be hoping to get his career back on track. He had a disappointing season at Chelsea - which I know all about - but I do think there's a player in there and hopefully he'll he'll suit Forest.

It will be interesting to see who plays as that central striker. With the money they've spent on Delap then Chris Wood may not play a major role.

I thought Liverpool deserved a point at least at Newcastle and they got a fair bit of criticism but I can't see past the Liverpool win and I think Alexander Isak will get off the mark.

Last season he shot himself in the foot - forcing the move and then he had injury issues and it didn't quite happen for him. We know there's a player in there and for his sake and Liverpool 's sake the sooner he comes to the fore the better.

Ben's prediction: This is a home win for Liverpool . 2-0

Bournemouth were resolute against Manchester City last week and they took the lead. The way in which they lost with the two late goals would have felt a real gut-wrencher for them.

Everton are off to a bit of a flyer under David Moyes - beating Palace and then Preston North End in the EFL Cup.

It will be interesting to see how Thierno Barry gets on because got a hat-trick against Preston in the Cup in midweek and I thought he was a bit of a nuisance last year to play against. He's still raw but I think he's got something.

I fancy Everton more than Bournemouth but I'm going to go for the draw.

Ben's prediction: Everton are going to nick this. 1-2

I thought Andros Townsend was a bit harsh on Coventry on the Monday Night Club talking about the way they were beaten by Arsenal . I think Arsenal have the best team, the best squad and I don't think we can really judge Coventry on that.

Dean Holden - Hull's assistant manager - has talked about the way that Hull were going to play and then they go and back it up and beat Manchester United in the way that they did.

I think seven or eight of the team were playing in the Championship last season so this is a big game because you can imagine Coventry fans thinking this is a great chance at home to get three points after a tough start.

But Hull will go into this thinking if they can go back-to-back then what a start that is because they've been written off by idiots like myself. But I am going to edge Coventry at home.

Ben's prediction: This has worked out in my favour, having two promoted teams playing each other. It's going to be a cagey game because they will both want to get over each other, but I can see Coventry coming out on top. 1-0

We all thought this was going to be Tottenham 's season but their defeat by Brentford was one of the extreme results at the weekend.

Roberto de Zerbi's said after the game that the players weren't fit enough, lost all the duels, weren't physical enough then used excuses about the pre-season and players coming in after the World Cup.

It looks like Newcastle are going to be the counter-attack kings this season. They've brought Nico Gonzalez in but whether he'll start I'm not sure but they have got pace as well.

Anthony Elanga scored last week having not scored at all in the Premier League last season but I have to say I haven't got a clue what this will be. I'm going to go for a Spurs win but I couldn't tell you why.

Ben's prediction: Spurs had a terrible season last time but they have had so many good players come in, while Newcastle have kind of done the opposite. Still, I am basing my prediction on Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi because I watched him so many times at Brighton - and I am going for a draw. 2-2

Brighton are off to a flying start and it was a great opening result and performance by Xabi Alonso's Chelsea , winning the west London derby against Fulham .

Chelsea have got some talented players and, because they've got no European football, they're going to have a good crack in the Premier League this season.

What interested me against Fulham is Chelsea didn't have a lot of possession, but they were effective when they did have possession.

But Brighton are just one of those teams. I don't think I predicted a single Brighton result right last season they're just impossible to call.

I really like Jack Hinshelwood he's such an exciting young player and there's a good history with his family in football and connection to Brighton .

But I'm going to say Chelsea carry on this run and get the three points.

Ben's prediction: I have to go with my team. It is going to be close - well, actually I don't know if it will be close... but I have just got to go with it. 1-2

Ben on which Brighton players will shine this season: We have managed to hang on to Bart Verbruggen, which was massive, and we have still got Georginio Rutter, who scored an amazing goal in pre-season against Roma, and then there is also Yasin Ayari.

But I've heard some amazing things about our Greek players Charalampos Kostoulas and Stefanos Tzimas, who we did not see much of last season. They will be like new signings for us.

Leeds and Daniel Farke proved loads of people wrong last season. But they were pretty cagey against Nottingham Forest last week in the Premier League.

They weren't very creative but then they got the job done against them in the EFL Cup in midweek and because of that I can't see Leeds losing.

Brentford are off to an absolute flyer - smashing Tottenham then hitting Birmingham for six or seven. They've started well with all the talk about their new midfielder Mamadou Sangare who now looks a bargain.

I think this is going to be really tight because Brentford like to play on the counter-attack.

Ben's prediction: This will definitely be close. 0-1

Sunderland need to get points on the board because they had a superb transfer window last summer but they've barely brought anybody in this year and their squad is going to be stretched because of Europe.

I got Sunderland really badly wrong last season but there's a lot of talk that they could be in trouble this year with so many games.

I still think they're good enough to stay up - they've got Granit Xhaka and some other good players. I like that they are physical and aggressive.

They made careless mistakes losing to Ipswich last week, giving the goals away, but I'm going to back Sunderland at home.

I think Fulham are going to be in a bit of bother this season, albeit they had some good spells against Chelsea last time out.

Ben's prediction: Sunderland 's home crowd will lift them again - look how strong they were at the Stadium of Light last season. 2-0

Well done to Ipswich for their start. It took them 11 games to get the first win under Kieran McKenna the last time they were in the Premier League and they've got off to a great start already.

Under Gary O'Neil they have got a bit about them - they've got players who can get them up the pitch, they have got pace with Daizen Maeda and Emersonn looks a bit of a handful.

I think they could cause United one or two problems but it's unthinkable that Manchester United could lose their opening two games of the season. Their start was an absolute stinker - they were very flat against Hull.

With respect, it was an open goal start for the season for them, with Hull then Ipswich - two promoted sides - and it would be bordering on catastrophic for Michael Carrick if they lose again.

I remember the days when United used to beat Ipswich 9-0 but I don't think it will be nine and I think Ipswich will score. I think Ipswich will score first but United will come from behind to win - panic over, Carrick's the king again.

Ben's prediction: As much as I'd like to say Ipswich will win this, they won't. 2-0

I'm a massive fan of Unai Emery but the Ollie Watkins thing sickens you a bit, he was really let down by his striker last week.

Aston Villa had a slow start last season, they have lost big players and I just think Arsenal are going to run all over teams this season.

Physically the will be too strong and they played some good stuff against Coventry. I think they are going to get better and better which is ominous for everybody else.

I wouldn't totally rule Emery and Villa out of it because you just don't know. They're very principled in the way they play, probably the most principled team in the Premier League in the way that they build from the back.

But I think Arsenal will swarm all over them.

Ben's prediction: Arsenal to take it, just about. 1-2

The collective efforts of the BBC Sport readers predicted two exact scores and one correct result to record 90 points .

All four contestants last week correctly predicted a 3-0 win for Arsenal over Coventry and Chris added three correct results to that to tally 70 points .

articles.title: Dundee United bids for Falkirk's Brad Spencer 'embarassing' says John McGlynn
articles.summary: Dundee United should be "embarrassed" by the bids they have made for midfielder Brad Spencer, says Falkirk manager John McGlynn.
articles.body:
Dundee United should be "embarrassed" by the bids they have made for midfielder Brad Spencer, says Falkirk manager John McGlynn.

McGlynn reveals Falkirk have rejected three offers from their fellow Scottish Premiership outfit for the 30-year-old, who has almost two years left on his contract and the option for a further 12 months.

Those bids have been reported to be , external worth six figures, however McGlynn says they are not enough.

"We have continuously told them for some time now that Brad's not for sale," he said. "I don't think it would matter [if Dundee United came back], they are miles off, embarrassing.

"I know the guy who wrote them and he must have been embarrassed when he was writing these offers, he must have been embarrassed.

"You wouldn't want your best player going to one of your direct opponents while they're under contract and Brad's got at least another couple of years on his contract, so they are kidding themselves on basically.

"From a football point of view we're saying that Brad will be here, he's under contract, unless the board accept it and they are not going to accept their offer."

articles.title: York Knights: Local ownership group led by David Dickson agree to buy majority share of Super League club
articles.summary: New local ownership group agree to buy majority share of club; Outgoing chairman and chief executive Clint Goodchild believes "the club is in safe hands and has a very bright future"
articles.body:
The group is headed by York businessman David Dickson and his family with the transfer of ownership for both York Knights and York Valkyrie currently progressing and pending formal approval by the Rugby Football League.

York Knights won promotion to Super League for the first time at the end of last season and are 12th in the table.

York Valkyrie won consecutive Women's Super League titles in 2023 and 2024 and currently sit third in this year's table.

Clint Goodchild has stepped down as chairman and CEO, with current general manager Neil Gulliver to become chief executive. Richard Larking remains on the board as a director.

A York RLFC statement read: "The club would like to put on record their appreciation and thanks to Clint Goodchild for his time as custodian of the club.

"His vision, ambition and drive saw the club progress during his tenure at an incredible pace.

"Following a successful re-brand of the club, unprecedented on field success followed with York Valkyrie securing back-to-back Betfred Women's Super League titles and York Knights not only winning the AB Sundecks 1895 Cup at Wembley, but also gaining promotion to the Betfred Super League in 2026 for the very first time in their history.

"The rapid growth and recent successes of the club has brought immense pride to the city, with the incoming ownership group being fully committed to enhancing the club's future, building on these strong foundations, and unlocking York Knights' true potential.

"Over the coming weeks the club will outline their strategic plans and vision as the 2026 season reaches its climax and preparations for 2027 begin."

Goodchild said: "I brought ambition. I leave with enough friendships and memories to last a lifetime.

"On arrival I knew York was a proud rugby league city, but I didn't know then how much this place, this club and its people would come to mean to me.

"To the players who sacrifice their bodies. The coaches who demand more. The staff who care far beyond their job descriptions. The volunteers who give their time. The sponsors and partners who believe. And the supporters who keep turning up. Thank you for believing. Together we made history.

"The club is in safe hands and has a very bright future. The club is lucky to have such a wonderful Yorkshire family involved and I am excited for this next York RLFC chapter."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: De '¿Quién quiere ser millonario?' a enfrentarse al Barça en Champions
articles.standfirst: La historia de Valdas Dambrauskas, el técnico del Sabah FK
articles.summary: La historia de Valdas Dambrauskas, el técnico del Sabah FK
articles.body: Hay historias que parecen de película. Y la historia de Valdas Dambrauskas es una de ellas. Y su clasificación para la Champions League con el Sabah FK es el momento de clímax de la función. Y más épica añadida gracias a la forma en la que se clasificaron. El técnico lituano ha pasado por clubes reconocidos de Europa, como Zalgiris, Ludogorets o Omonia Nicosia, entro otros. Pero el cómo llegó hasta ahí, es lo más curioso de todo. Su historia, lejos del fútbol, comenzó en su país, en 2002, cuando participó en la versión lituana de '¿Quién quiere ser millonario?', el famoso concurso televisivo que en España también se hizo. Tenía 25 años, una licenciatura en ingeniería y no había llegado a jugar profesionalmente al fútbol. Sin embargo, tenía muy claro a que quería dedicarse. Estaba dispuesto a llevarse el premio máximo, aunque al final terminó ganando 4000 litas, lo que al cambio al euro actual son 1158 euros. Puede parecer poco, pero fue suficiente para comenzar su historia. "Era el equivalente a un salario anual en Lituania. Con esa cantidad de dinero, podías cubrir dos años de matrícula", explicó a Four Four Two. Sin embargo, decidió perseguir su sueño. Se marchó con su novia a Inglaterra y comenzó a cursar un grado en Ciencias del Deporte y Entrenamiento en la London Metropolitan University. "Desde los 12 años, cuando me di cuenta de que no sería futbolista profesional, supe que quería ser entrenador de fútbol. Se dio la posibilidad de mudarme a Inglaterra. Fui en busca de una vida mejor, pero con la idea clara de intentar abrirme camino como entrenador. Estoy muy feliz de poder trabajar en el fútbol y convertirlo en mi profesión. No puedo adivinar qué habría pasado sin ese concurso, pero creo que habría encontrado la manera de cumplir mi sueño", comentó a Flashcore. "Después de pagar los vuelos y el alojamiento, nos quedaba dinero para cubrir nuestros gastos de solo un mes, así que necesitaba encontrar un trabajo a tiempo parcial urgentemente", comentó. Y así fue, comenzó a trabajar en un centro comercial. Pero su gran oportunidad llegó. El Manchester United le abrió las puertas de su academia. "Por aquel entonces todavía no hablaba bien inglés, pero les gusté por mi personalidad y conseguí el trabajo. Venir de Lituania y que me dieran esa oportunidad supuso un gran paso para mí", recordaba a FFT. Más tarde, comenzó como entrenador del London Tigers y de la cantera del Fulham. "Fue una experiencia fantástica; todos mis trabajos formaron parte de un gran proceso de aprendizaje", añadía a FFT. Con el paso del tiempo, fue llamando la atención de la selección nacional, y comenzó a entrenar diferentes categorías inferiores de Lituania. Fui a todos los cursos y conferencias posibles para mejorar. Luego empecé a soñar y planear cómo conseguir un puesto en el fútbol profesional. Sabía que en Inglaterra sería imposible, pero que tendría una oportunidad en mi país", afirmó a Flashcore. Su primera experiencia al frente de un banquillo profesional fue en su país. Tras unos años siendo asistente de Valdas Urbonas en el Ekranas Panevezys, en 2013 asumió el reto de dirigir al primer equipo. Aunque solo fue el principio de su carrera. A finales de 2014, fichó por el Zalgiris, con el que conquistó sus primeros títulos, dos Ligas, dos Copas y dos Supercopas. Además, es hasta el momento el club al que más ha dirigido con 118 encuentros. Continuó su carrera por RFS, HNK Gorica, Ludogorets, Hadjuk Split, OFI Creta, Omonia Nicosia y Diosgyor, ganando por el camino Copa de Letonia, Liga y Supercopa de Bulgaria y Copa de Croacia. Y en 2025 llegó al club con el que llega a la élite europea, el Sabah FK. El club de Azerbaiyán solo había conquistado un título en sus nueve años de historia, la Copa justo antes de la llegada del Lituano. En el primer curso de Dambrauskas en el banquillo, conquistó el doblete de Liga y Copa, dándole la posibilidad de disputar las eliminatorias de Champions. Superaron a The New Saints Football Club, Kuopion Palloseura y Aarhus. Se plantaron el la última ronda contra el Hapoel Be'er Sheva. Perdieron el partido de ida 2-1 y en el de vuelta, caían 1-2 en el 73. Sin embargo, consiguieron empatar la eliminatoria en el 94 y con dos goles en la prórroga, se han clasificado para la fase de grupos de la Champions League, donde se enfrentarán a todo un gigante del continente como el Barcelona y al Villarreal. Una historia de cine la de Valdas Dambrauskas, de participar en un concurso televisivo, a entrenar en la máxima competición europea.

articles.title: Rivales del Betis en el sorteo de Champions: cita con los campeones de la Premier y la Bundesliga
articles.standfirst: Los verdiblancos jugarán ante Arsenal, Bayern Munich, Porto, Dortmund, Feyenoord, Lille, Como y Slovan Bratislava
articles.summary: Los verdiblancos jugarán ante Arsenal, Bayern Munich, Porto, Dortmund, Feyenoord, Lille, Como y Slovan Bratislava
articles.body: El Real Betis Balompié regresa a la Champions League, la máxima competición del fútbol continental de clubes, más de 20 años después la que hasta la fecha era su primera y única presencia en el torneo. Y lo hace con un camino que ha quedado establecido esta tarde tras el sorteo de la Fase de Liga celebrado en el Grimaldi Forum de Mónaco, donde ha conocido cuáles serán sus ocho rivales y qué partidos jugará en casa, en el Estadio de La Cartuja, y a domicilio: Los campeones de la Premier League, el Arsenal, y de la Bundesliga, el Bayern Munich, además del Porto y el Borussia Dortmund se presentan como los adversarios más duros para los verdiblancos. El calendario definitivo con fechas y horarios se conocerá antes del sábado, pero la marea verdiblanca se prepara ya para volver a dejar su sello en el Viejo Continente con desplazamientos masivos, entre otros estadios, al Allianz Arena alemán. El equipo de Pellegrini, una vez conocidos los adversarios con los que se verá las caras en esta primera fase de la competición, tratará de hacerse fuerte en su estadio para intentar alcanzar por primera vez en su historia las rondas eliminatorias de la Liga de Campeones. En su anterior participación en el torneo, cuando aún se disputaba una fase de grupos, quedó eliminado después de sumar siete puntos con dos triunfos, un empate y tres derrotas. Dos de los rivales más duros para el Betis, que tendrá un camino muy complicado en busca de las eliminatorias, serán los campeones de la Premier y la Bundesliga. Al Arsenal se enfrentó en pretemporada el equipo de Pellegrini en Irlanda, ganando 1-3, pero con la ausencia de la mayoría de mundialistas. Además de recibir en casa al equipo de Mikel Arteta, que cuenta con una amplia representación española con jugadores como David Raya, Zubimendi o Mikel Merino, los verdiblancos tendrán que visitar en Allianz Arena para verse las caras por primera vez en partido oficial con el Bayern Munich. En sus duelos ante los rivales de su mismo bombo, el 2, tampoco ha acompañado la suerte al conjunto andaluz. Recibirá en La Cartuja al Porto, un equipo dos veces campeón de Europa con una plantilla valorada en más de 400 millones de euros según transfermarkt de la que forman parte los españoles Gabri Veiga y Samu. Y además, tendrá que visitar el complicadísimo Westfalenstadion para verse las caras con el Borussia Dortmund, finalista de la competición en la 2023-24 y subcampeón de la pasada Bundesliga. Los de Pellegrini intentarán buscar en La Cartuja los puntos que les permitan soñar con pasar a las eliminatorias. Pero donde estará la clave, principalmente, será ante los rivales de los bombos 3 y 4 del sorteo. El Feyenoord, subcampeón de la Eredivisie 2025-26, visitará el recinto sevillano por segunda temporada consecutiva tras caer 2-1 a finales de enero de este año y quedarse fuera de la fase de liga de la Europa League. Mientras que a los verdiblancos les tocará viajar a Francia para enfrentarse al Lille, tercero de la Ligue 1 el pasado curso, que alcanzó los octavos del segundo torneo continental hace un año. Por último, en su regreso a la Champions más de 20 años después, el Betis se medirá en casa a un debutante en la competición, el Como italiano dirigido por Cesc Fábregas y del que forman parte dos exbéticos, Jesús Rodríguez y Assane Diao, además de otros españoles como Álex Valle y Luis Milla; y viajará a Eslovaquia para la que, en teoría, se presenta como su salida más 'asequible', ante el Slovan Bratislava, que viene de jugar la Conference el pasado curso.

articles.title: Kareem Tunde, nuevo jugador del West Bromwich Albion
articles.standfirst: El canterano granota se marcha por un traspaso tasado en tres millones de euros y el 25% de una futura venta
articles.summary: El canterano granota se marcha por un traspaso tasado en tres millones de euros y el 25% de una futura venta
articles.body: El Levante ha hecho oficial el traspasado de Kareem Tunde al West Bromwich Albion de la Championship inglesa. El canterano granota, gran protagonista de la segunda vuelta de la pasada temporada, se marcha por una cantidad de tres millones y el 25% de una futura venta. La irrupción del atacante se produjo, de manera significativa, con la llegada de Luís Castro a la disciplina del equipo del barrio de Orriols, siendo fundamental en la permanencia del equipo en la máxima categoría del fútbol español, llegando a disputar un total de 21 partidos oficiales. El jugador catalán ha querido mostrar su gratitud al Levante dando, "las gracias por la confianza, por las experiencias y por todos los momentos vividos". Así mismo ha querido agradecer a "cada entrenador y miembro de los cuerpos técnicos, a mis compañeros, a los tutores y a Guaita". A su vez, ha querido subrayar el aprendizaje durante estos últimos cinco años y ha destacado la oportunidad de madurar y "ser un jugador mucho más preparado". Y ha querido concluir, mostrando su orgullo por "haber defendido este escudo y agradecido por haber formado parte de esta familia".

articles.title: Al Barça le toca otra vez el campeón
articles.standfirst: El Barça vuelve a enfrentarse al PSG y al City de Haaland
articles.summary: El Barça vuelve a enfrentarse al PSG y al City de Haaland
articles.body: El Barcelona volverá a verse las caras con el campeón, el PSG. A pesar de ello salió bien parado del sorteo de la liguilla de la Champions League. Es cierto que los dos rivales del bombo 1 son muy fuertes, pero cualquier rival era muy potente. El morbo es el enfrentamiento con el PSG, al igual que sucediera la temporada. El resto de rivales no han sido de los más difíciles que les podría haber tocado. El conjunto azulgrana se verá las caras frente a un clásico como es el Manchester City, aunque esta vez ya no estará Pep Guardiola en el banquillo. La amenaza será como siempre en este equipo Erling Haaland. Y aquí el morbo es Rodri frente a su exequipo. El otro conjunto del bombo 1 es también un clásico porque el equipo azulgrana volverá a enfrentarse al PSG, actual campeón del torneo, como sucediera la pasada campaña. El morbo en este partido será la presencia de Ferran Torres, recientemente traspasado al club francés. La calidad del equipo parisino es incuestionable con jugadores como Dembélé, Marquiños, Fabián, Kvaratskhelia o Doué El Aston Villa de Emery es una amenaza a tener en cuenta. La ventaja es que el partido se disputará en el Spotify Camp Nou. La diferencia es importante si el partido se hubiera tenido que disputar en Inglaterra. El Sporting de Portugal, era uno de los rivales más asequibles del bombo 2. El Barcelona parte como favorito con los otros cuatro rivales que tienen. Hay que destacar el regreso de Cesc Fábregas al Camp Nou. Lo hará esta vez como entrenador del Como que la pasada campaña fue una auténtica revelación de la Serie A. Los otros tres son Galatasaray, Feyenoord y Sabah.

articles.summary: Toca y toca el Barça esperando a ver si el Athletic decide salir a buscarle y dejar metros a su espalda. Doble cambio en el Athletic. Entran Gerenabar
articles.body:
Última hora del Barcelona - Athletic en directo:

¡¡Muuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuy buenas tardes a todos y bienvenidos a una nueva jornada de LaLiga EA Sports en MARCA.com!! En aproximadamente dos horas tenemos partidazo en el Spotify Camp Nou . El primero en el feudo catalán esta temporada. El Barça de Hansi Flick recibe al Athletic de Terzic con la obligación de ganar para seguir la estela del Real Madrid, que ya es líder tras su goleada ayer a la Real Sociedad.

Llegan los azulgrana en un estado de confianza alta tras su convincente estreno ante el Elche . Con el ruido del mercado y Julián Álvarez de fondo, y con el sorteo de Champions recién salido del horno (ahora comentamos), el equipo catalán espera disfrutar de una gran noche de fútbol con un gran aliciente: el debut de Rodri. El centrocampista, en principio, tendrá minutos en el segundo tiempo.

Y todo esto con la visita de un Athletic que llega de capa caída tras su decepcionante debut en San Mamés . Cayó ante el Sevilla con claridad, sufrió la primera decisión polémica de la temporada con la expulsión de Yuri y visita un estadio que no se le da precisamente bien en los últimos tiempos. Todo en contra, a priori, para un equipo que suele sacar su mejor versión en los momentos duros. Y hoy es uno de ellos.

Desde ya mismo les iremos contando todo lo que suceda en Barcelona: alineaciones oficiales, ambiente previo, datos y estadísticas... ¿Se animan a vivirlo con nosotros? ¡Venga que eeeeeeeeeeeempezamos!

articles.title: UEFA pursuing legal action against FIFA, president Gianni Infantino, withdraws World Cup boycott threat
articles.summary: UEFA says the claims relate to alleged criminal mismanagement.
articles.body:
UEFA is taking legal action in New York against FIFA, Gianni Infantino and Thrive Capital, the lead investor in the failed $20 billion World Cup investment plan, according to The Times and Front Office Sports .

This is not a lawsuit. UEFA, instead, is wanting to go through the discovery process to get information from the three parties in order to take that to Swiss authorities — FIFA's headquarters are in Switzerland — as part of a criminal complaint. The end goal is to have charges brought against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials.

Infantino is accused of "fraudulently" offering a stake in the FIFA Forward Enterprise without going through the proper FIFA channels.

Thrive and founder Joshua Kushner were set to pay FIFA $4.2 billion for a 20% stake in a new company that would run the organization's commercial events, which includes the men's and women's World Cup.

"Under the terms Infantino announced, those investors stood to acquire a permanent financial interest in FIFA's commercial arm for $4.2bn, implying an absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn, a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer," UEFA's complaint reads.

That $4.2 billion figure could be a "fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit," it adds.

"In truth, it was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA's most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family," the complaint continued. "Infantino pushed the plan through internal FIFA approval only days earlier at a hastily convened meeting where a limited number of FIFA's management officials and employees — some of whom had never heard of the plan — were given mere hours to sign off on an unprecedented multi-billion dollar scheme."

"In truth, it was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA's most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family," the complaint continued.

"Infantino pushed the plan through internal FIFA approval only days earlier at a hastily convened meeting where a limited number of FIFA's management officials and employees — some of whom had never heard of the plan — were given mere hours to sign off on an unprecedented multi-billion dollar scheme."

Infantino's received criticism from all corners of the soccer world after The Times reported the details of the plan. Various confederations, including UEFA and Concacaf, issued scathing statements against the FIFA president with a number calling for " meaningful change " atop the governing body's hierarchy.

UEFA, which released a statement saying it had lost confidence in Infantino's ability to lead, threatened to boycott all FIFA-run competitions unless FIFA issued assurances that the sell off plan would not be revisited.

UEFA has withdrawn its plans to boycott FIFA-run competitions after the European soccer governing body was told Infantino's plan will not be revived.

"The delegates were also informed that FIFA has now confirmed in writing to UEFA that the FIFA Forward Enterprise project has been 'irrevocably and permanently withdrawn' and that it 'will not re-appear in any other shape, construction, name or form,'" read a statement from UEFA on Thursday . "Having now secured the two assurances it required from FIFA on 30 July, and following consultation with its National Associations, UEFA has therefore agreed to suspend, on a provisional basis, the withdrawal by European teams from FIFA competitions in the coming season, including the Women's U20 World Cup, U17 World Cup and the Women's U17 World Cup. This position will remain under constant review and may be reconsidered immediately if circumstances so require. "While the immediate question of participation has now been resolved, the underlying crisis has not. "The abandonment of FFE does not erase the deception, intimidation and abuse of power that made it possible. Nor does it restore the confidence that has been lost. "This is not a choice between good governance and football development. Nor is this about Europe seeking greater power within FIFA. It is simply about ensuring that no part of world football – large or small, those with more and those with less – is dependent on the power of one individual."

"The delegates were also informed that FIFA has now confirmed in writing to UEFA that the FIFA Forward Enterprise project has been 'irrevocably and permanently withdrawn' and that it 'will not re-appear in any other shape, construction, name or form,'" read a statement from UEFA on Thursday .

"Having now secured the two assurances it required from FIFA on 30 July, and following consultation with its National Associations, UEFA has therefore agreed to suspend, on a provisional basis, the withdrawal by European teams from FIFA competitions in the coming season, including the Women's U20 World Cup, U17 World Cup and the Women's U17 World Cup. This position will remain under constant review and may be reconsidered immediately if circumstances so require.

"While the immediate question of participation has now been resolved, the underlying crisis has not.

"The abandonment of FFE does not erase the deception, intimidation and abuse of power that made it possible. Nor does it restore the confidence that has been lost.

"This is not a choice between good governance and football development. Nor is this about Europe seeking greater power within FIFA. It is simply about ensuring that no part of world football – large or small, those with more and those with less – is dependent on the power of one individual."

The 55 member nations of UEFA met in Monaco on Thursday ahead of the 2026-27 Champions League draw . Calling off the planned boycott ensures no issues for the upcoming FIFA Under-20 Women's World Cup, which will begin Sept. 5 in Poland.

FIFA released a statement saying it "strongly believes that football has the power to unite, even in challenging circumstances, and looks forward to welcoming all teams and players to Poland."

As UEFA calls off its boycott, the Italian and Romanian football federations joined the growing list of countries to withdraw support of Infantino.

The FIGC's statement on Wednesday said that it would no longer support Infantino's reelection in March due to "the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning governance and the development of international competitions."

"FIFA needs today a new leader who can produce consensus and unity, inspire trust and who has the ability to bring us all together," President Răzvan Burleanu of Romania's FRF said.

articles.summary: El Betis y el Villarreal lo tendrán complicado para meterse en el top 24 con rivales muy potentes enfrente
articles.body: El sorteo de la fase liga de la Champions trajo duelos con morbo para los cinco equipos españoles que afrontarán estos ocho partidos con la esperanza de colarse en los octavos de final y luego pelear una Liga de Campeones cuya final se disputará el 5 de junio en el estadio Metropolitano de Madrid. El Real Madrid tuvo algo más de suerte que un Barça y Atlético que tendrán duros rivales para meterse en octavos. Betis y Villarreal también se encontrarán con equipos complicados en su camino para clasificarse en el top 24. El Real Madrid fue la primera bola en salir y los blancos evitaron a los peces gordos del bombo de los cabezas de serie, ya que se encontrarán en su camino con el Inter (casa), Arsenal (fuera), PSV (c), Roma (f), Leipzig (c), Shakhtar (f), Lask (c) y AEK Atenas (f). El Barcelona fue menos afortunado en el sorteo y en su camino se encontrará al campeón PSG en el Parque de los Príncipes, con el morbo de Ferran y Luis Enrique. Los otros rivales serán el Manchester City, con Rodri midiéndose a su exequipo, Aston Villa, Feyenoord y Como en casa y Sporting de Portugal, Galatasaray y Sabah lejos del Camp Nou. El Atlético de Madrid se medirá al Bayern, Manchester United, Fenerbahçe y Viking en casa y Liverpool, PSV, Bodo y Stuttgart fuera, por lo que el camino tampoco será sencillo para los de Simeone en su deseo de meterse directamente en octavos de final. El Betis de Pellegrini, que vuelve 20 años después a la máxima competición continental, tendrá duros rivales en su objetivo de colarse en el top 24: Arsenal (c), Bayern Múnich (f), Oporto (c), Borussia Dortmund (f), Feyenoord (c), Lille (f), Como (c) y Slovan Bratislava (f). En el bombo 3 la representación española era la del Villarreal, que repite participación con la idea de mejorar la mala fase liga del año pasado, y que se medirá a PSG, Manchester United, Napoles y Sabah en casa y Liverpool, Borussia Dortmund, Fenerbahce y Slavia Praga fuera. Este sábado se conocerán las fechas y horarios de las ocho jornadas de esta fase liga que comenzará el martes 8 de septiembre y finalizará el 27 de enero de 2027. articles.title: Bill Belichick Reveals if He'd Return to NFL Ahead of 2nd CFB Season as UNC HC
articles.summary: UNC football head coach Bill Belichick, who is entering his second season with the Tar Heels after a 49-year stint in the NFL, was asked on Thursday whether he would consider returning to the pros. He provided the following response.
articles.body:
UNC football head coach Bill Belichick, who is entering his second season with the Tar Heels after a 49-year stint in the NFL, was asked on Thursday whether he would consider returning to the pros. He provided the following response.

Belichick made his remarks from Ireland, where the Tar Heels will open the season on Saturday against TCU in Dublin.

Belichick signed a five-year, $50 million contract to become UNC's next head coach. However, the final two seasons of the contract aren't guaranteed.

His first season went poorly. UNC went 4-8 and 2-6 in the ACC. Five of the Tar Heels' losses were by 16 or more points.

On Oct. 8, 2025, Belichick reaffirmed his commitment to the Tar Heels, and UNC athletic director Bubba Cunningham announced his full support as well.

One month later, the New York Giants' head coaching job opened after the team parted ways with Brian Daboll. Belichick was the New York Giants' defensive coordinator from 1983-1990 and won two Super Bowls with the organization.

Speculation, of course, connected Belichick to the Giants, and he released another statement confirming his commitment to UNC.

"Despite circulating rumors, I have not and will not pursue any NFL head coaching vacancies," Belichick said in part.

Belichick did express his great respect for the Mara and Tisch families, who co-own the team, but he told the public he was remaining in Chapel Hill.

"We have tremendous support from the university, our alumni, and the entire Carolina community. My focus remains solely on continuing to improve this team, develop our players, and build a program that makes Tar Heel fans proud."

UNC has endured a difficult offseason. Of note, general manager Michael Lombardi, who previously worked with Belichick in the NFL, being placed on paid administrative leave .

Belichick's oldest son, UNC defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, is unfortunately out indefinitely on medical leave.

UNC landed 15th out of 17 teams in the ACC's preseason poll , which consisted of 185 credentialed media members' opinions about the conference's order of finish.

We'll see how the Tar Heels do soon enough, though, beginning Saturday. Their first ACC game will be on Saturday, Sept. 19 at Clemson.

articles.title: Julián Calero pone de ejemplo al Aston Villa para motivar a su Oviedo
articles.standfirst: Y avisó del nivel de su próximo rival: "el Albacete es un equipo con potencial para pelear por cosas"
articles.summary: Y avisó del nivel de su próximo rival: "el Albacete es un equipo con potencial para pelear por cosas"
articles.body: Julián Calero, técnico del Real Oviedo, compareció en la previa del encuentro que los azules jugarán el sábado en el Carlos Belmonte ante un Albacete al que el preparador azul considera "un equipo con potencial para pelear por cosas". "El Albacete no lleva puntos, pero en mi opinión han hecho una plantilla muy competitiva. A nivel de confianza ninguno llegamos plenos, pero sí somos dos equipos que tenemos clara la idea y que hacemos muchas cosas bien. Será difícil y también hará calor, por lo que habrá que adaptarse", explicó el entrenador carbayón en la sala de prensa de El Requexón, tras el penúltimo entrenamiento de la semana.. El Oviedo ha sumado un solo punto en las dos primeras jornadas del curso, ambas disputadas en el Carlos Tartiere, pero Calero aseguró que existen "rachas en las que cuesta más todo" y que los azules, a pesar de empatar ante el Granada y perder ante el Leganés, son uno de los equipos "que más ha tirado y que menos tiros ha permitido". "Le he hablado a los jugadores del Aston Villa, que en la jornada 4ª del año pasado iba en descenso, acabó en Champions League y ganó la Europa League. Una especie de símil para entender que las cosas a veces no empiezan como quieres", comentó el entrenador parleño. Preguntado por el mercado de fichajes, que cierra el próximo martes por la noche, Calero fue muy claro diciendo que "los entornos vuelven locos a los jugadores y en las últimas horas del mercado se agrava, así que la misión de un cuerpo técnico es apostar por los futbolistas que están concentrados al 100%". El Real Oviedo, que ante el Albacete tendrá las bajas seguras de Ilyas Chaira y un Marco Esteban que volvió a entrenar con el grupo, completará este viernes a primera hora su última sesión de trabajo antes de viajar a tierras manchegas, donde hará noche de viernes a sábado
